fields.name: COUNT
fields.text: Set when the counter has reached 0 since the register was last read; a read of STCTRL or any write to STCURRENT clears it. A debugger read through the DAP clears it only while MasterType in the AHB-AP Control Register is 0, and otherwise leaves it unchanged.

values.text: No count to 0 since the last read.
Counter has reached 0 since the last read.

fields.name: CLK_SRC
fields.text: Selects the clock that drives the SysTick counter.

fields.name: INTEN
fields.text: Enables the SysTick interrupt at count 0.

values.text: No interrupt; software can poll COUNT to see whether the counter has reached 0.
SysTick raises an interrupt to the NVIC on reaching 0.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Starts and stops the SysTick counter.

values.text: Counter runs repeatedly: it loads RELOAD, counts down, sets COUNT and raises the interrupt if INTEN is set on reaching 0, then reloads and counts again.

fields.name: RELOAD
fields.text: Start value copied into STCURRENT each time the counter reaches 0.

fields.name: CURRENT
fields.text: Counter value at the moment of access; there is no read-modify-write protection. Any write clears it to 0 and also clears STCTRL.COUNT.

fields.name: INTID
fields.text: Writing an interrupt number here triggers that interrupt by software; 0x3 triggers IRQ3.

fields.name: DISOOFP
fields.text: When set, floating-point instructions no longer complete out of order relative to integer instructions.

fields.name: DISFPCA
fields.text: When set, the FPCA bit of CONTROL is no longer updated automatically. Whether FPCA can be enabled depends on both this bit and FPCC.ASPEN.

fields.name: DISFOLD
fields.text: Turns off IT folding, in which the processor begins the first instruction of an IT block while still executing the IT instruction. Folding speeds execution but can add jitter to loops; set this bit before a task that must not jitter.

fields.name: DISWBUF
fields.text: Stops the write buffer being used for accesses to the default memory map.

values.text: Write buffer not used for default memory map accesses: every bus fault is precise, but each store must finish before the next instruction runs, which lowers performance. Only the Cortex-M4's own write buffers are affected.

fields.name: DISMCYC
fields.text: Stops load-multiple and store-multiple instructions being interrupted.

values.text: LDM and STM are not interrupted; each must finish before the processor stacks state and enters a handler, which raises interrupt latency.

fields.name: IMP
fields.text: Code of the processor's implementer.

fields.name: VAR
fields.text: Major revision of the processor.

values.text: The r value of the rNpN revision, as 0 in r0p0.

fields.name: CON
fields.text: Fixed field.

fields.name: PARTNO
fields.text: Processor part number.

fields.name: REV
fields.text: Minor revision of the processor.

values.text: The p value of the rNpN revision, as 1 in r0p1.

fields.name: NMISET
fields.text: Makes the NMI exception pending. As NMI has the highest priority, the processor normally enters its handler as soon as it sees this bit set and clears it on entry; read inside the NMI handler it returns 1 only if the NMI signal was asserted again during that handler.

values.text: Read: NMI not pending. Write: ignored.
Read: NMI pending. Write: makes NMI pending.

fields.name: PENDSV
fields.text: The only way to make PendSV pending; writing 1 to UNPENDSV clears it.

values.text: Read: PendSV not pending. Write: ignored.
Read: PendSV pending. Write: makes PendSV pending.

fields.name: UNPENDSV
fields.text: Write-only bit that removes the pending state of PendSV; its read value is unknown.

fields.name: PENDSTSET
fields.text: Makes the SysTick exception pending; writing 1 to PENDSTCLR clears it.

values.text: Read: SysTick not pending. Write: ignored.
Read: SysTick pending. Write: makes SysTick pending.

fields.name: PENDSTCLR
fields.text: Write-only bit that removes the pending state of SysTick; its read value is unknown.

fields.name: ISRPRE
fields.text: Shows whether leaving the halted state will take an interrupt. Only valid in Debug mode; reads 0 outside it.

values.text: Release from halt takes no interrupt.
Release from halt takes an interrupt.

fields.name: ISRPEND
fields.text: Shows whether any interrupt other than NMI and the faults is pending.

fields.name: VECPEND
fields.text: Number of the pending, enabled exception with top priority; BASEPRI and FAULTMASK are taken into account, PRIMASK is not.

fields.name: RETBASE
fields.text: Shows whether other preempted exceptions remain active, for all interrupts except NMI and the faults. Only meaningful while an ISR runs (IPSR not 0).

values.text: Preempted active exceptions remain to run.
No exception is active, or the running one is the only active one.

fields.name: VECACT
fields.text: Exception number of the exception now active, coded as in VECPEND; 0 means the processor is in Thread mode. It equals IPSR.ISRNUM. Subtracting 16 gives the IRQ number that indexes ENn, DISn, PENDn, UNPENDn and PRIn.

fields.name: OFFSET
fields.text: Offset of the vector table from address 0x0000.0000. It must be aligned to the table's number of exception entries; with 138 interrupts that means a 1024-byte boundary.

fields.name: VECTKEY
fields.text: Write key protecting this register: a write changes the register only if it carries 0x05FA here. Reads return 0xFA05.

fields.name: ENDIANESS
fields.text: Data endianness; this part is little-endian only, so the bit is 0.

fields.name: PRIGROUP
fields.text: Sets where the INTx priority fields split into group priority and subpriority.

fields.name: SYSRESREQ
fields.text: Requests a system reset. Cleared automatically while the core resets; reads 0.

values.text: Resets the core and every on-chip peripheral except the Debug interface.

fields.name: VECTCLRACT
fields.text: Reserved for Debug; reads 0 and must be written 0, or the result is unpredictable.

fields.name: VECTRESET
fields.text: Reserved for Debug; reads 0 and must be written 0, or the result is unpredictable.

fields.name: SEVONPEND
fields.text: Chooses which pending events wake the processor from WFE. When an event or interrupt becomes pending, the event signal wakes the processor; if it is not in WFE, the event is held and affects the next WFE. SEV and external events also wake it.

values.text: Only enabled interrupts and events wake the processor; disabled interrupts do not.
Enabled events and every interrupt, disabled ones included, wake the processor.

fields.name: SLEEPDEEP
fields.text: Chooses the low-power mode.

fields.name: SLEEPEXIT
fields.text: Puts the processor to sleep on return from an ISR, so an interrupt-driven program need not return to an empty main loop.

values.text: Stay awake on return from Handler to Thread mode.
Go to sleep or deep sleep when an ISR returns to Thread mode.

fields.name: STKALIGN
fields.text: Stack alignment kept on exception entry; the processor records it in bit 9 of the stacked PSR and restores it on return.

fields.name: BFHFNMIGN
fields.text: Lets handlers at priority -1 and -2 (hard fault, NMI, and handlers escalated by FAULTMASK) ignore data bus faults from loads and stores. Safe only with the handler and its data held in fully safe memory; its usual use is probing system devices and bridges to find and fix control path problems.

values.text: Load and store data bus faults cause a lock-up.
Handlers at priority -1 and -2 ignore load and store data bus faults.

fields.name: DIV0
fields.text: Makes an SDIV or UDIV with divisor 0 fault or halt.

fields.name: UNALIGNED
fields.text: Traps unaligned halfword and word accesses. Unaligned LDM, STM, LDRD and STRD fault whatever this bit holds.

values.text: Trap; the access raises a usage fault.

fields.name: MAINPEND
fields.text: Lets unprivileged software access SWTRIG.

fields.name: BASETHR
fields.text: Sets when the processor may enter Thread mode.

values.text: Only while no exception is active.
From any level, as an EXC_RETURN value directs.

fields.name: USAGE
fields.text: Usage fault priority, 0 to 7; a smaller number is a higher priority.

fields.name: BUS
fields.text: Bus fault priority, 0 to 7; a smaller number is a higher priority.

fields.name: MEM
fields.text: Memory management fault priority, 0 to 7; a smaller number is a higher priority.

fields.name: SVC
fields.text: SVCall priority, 0 to 7; a smaller number is a higher priority.

fields.name: TICK
fields.text: SysTick exception priority, 0 to 7; a smaller number is a higher priority.

fields.name: PENDSV
fields.text: PendSV priority, 0 to 7; a smaller number is a higher priority.

fields.name: DEBUG
fields.text: Debug priority, 0 to 7; a smaller number is a higher priority.

fields.name: USAGE
fields.text: Enables the usage fault exception.

fields.name: BUS
fields.text: Enables the bus fault exception.

fields.name: MEM
fields.text: Enables the memory management fault exception.

fields.name: SVC
fields.text: Pending state of the SVC call exception; writable to change it.

fields.name: BUSP
fields.text: Pending state of the bus fault exception; writable to change it.

fields.name: MEMP
fields.text: Pending state of the memory management fault exception; writable to change it.

fields.name: USAGEP
fields.text: Pending state of the usage fault exception; writable to change it.

fields.name: TICK
fields.text: Active state of the SysTick exception; writable to change it; writing it without matching changes to the stacked content can make the processor raise a fault.

fields.name: PNDSV
fields.text: Active state of the PendSV exception; writable to change it; writing it without matching changes to the stacked content can make the processor raise a fault.

fields.name: MON
fields.text: Shows whether the Debug monitor is active.

fields.name: SVCA
fields.text: Active state of the SVC call exception; writable to change it; writing it without matching changes to the stacked content can make the processor raise a fault.

fields.name: USGA
fields.text: Active state of the usage fault exception; writable to change it; writing it without matching changes to the stacked content can make the processor raise a fault.

fields.name: BUSA
fields.text: Active state of the bus fault exception; writable to change it; writing it without matching changes to the stacked content can make the processor raise a fault.

fields.name: MEMA
fields.text: Active state of the memory management fault exception; writable to change it; writing it without matching changes to the stacked content can make the processor raise a fault.

fields.name: DIV0
fields.text: Usage fault from a divide by zero; the stacked return PC then points at the dividing instruction. The trap is enabled by CFGCTRL.DIV0. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: No divide-by-zero fault, or the trap is off.
An SDIV or UDIV ran with divisor 0.

fields.name: UNALIGN
fields.text: Usage fault from an unaligned access; the trap is enabled by CFGCTRL.UNALIGNED. Unaligned LDM, STM, LDRD and STRD fault whatever the setting. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: No unaligned access fault, or the trap is off.
An unaligned memory access was made.

fields.name: NOCP
fields.text: Usage fault from an attempt to access a coprocessor. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: INVPC
fields.text: Usage fault from an illegal load of the PC; the stacked return PC then points at the instruction that tried it. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: An illegal EXC_RETURN load to the PC was attempted, from an invalid context or EXC_RETURN value.

fields.name: INVSTAT
fields.text: Usage fault from illegal use of the EPSR; the stacked return PC then points at the offending instruction. An undefined instruction using the EPSR does not set it. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: An instruction made illegal use of the EPSR.

fields.name: UNDEF
fields.text: Usage fault from an instruction the processor cannot decode; the stacked return PC then points at it. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: BFARV
fields.text: Set after a bus fault whose address is known; later faults, such as a memory management fault, can clear it. If a bus fault escalates to a hard fault by priority, the hard fault handler must clear it, so that a stacked active bus fault handler does not return to an overwritten FAULTADDR. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: FAULTADDR does not hold a valid fault address.
FAULTADDR holds a valid fault address.

fields.name: BLSPERR
fields.text: Bus fault during floating-point lazy state preservation. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: A bus fault occurred during lazy state preservation.

fields.name: BSTKE
fields.text: Bus fault while stacking on exception entry. The SP is still adjusted, but the stacked context may be wrong, and no address goes to FAULTADDR. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: Stacking on exception entry caused one or more bus faults.

fields.name: BUSTKE
fields.text: Bus fault while unstacking on exception return, chained to the handler: the original return stack remains, the SP is not adjusted, no new save is made and no address goes to FAULTADDR. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: Unstacking on exception return caused one or more bus faults.

fields.name: IMPRE
fields.text: Asynchronous data bus error; no address goes to FAULTADDR. If it is detected while the current priority is above the bus fault priority, the fault waits pending until all higher-priority work returns. A precise fault before the handler is entered leaves both IMPRE and a precise status bit set. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: A data bus error occurred, and the stacked return address does not relate to the faulting instruction.

fields.name: PRECISE
fields.text: Precise data bus error; the fault address goes to FAULTADDR. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: A data bus error occurred, and the stacked return PC points at the faulting instruction.

fields.name: IBUS
fields.text: Instruction bus error, detected at prefetch but flagged only when the processor tries to issue the faulting instruction; no address goes to FAULTADDR. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: MMARV
fields.text: Shows whether MMADDR holds a valid address. If a memory management fault escalates to a hard fault by priority, the hard fault handler must clear it, so that a stacked active memory management fault handler does not return to an overwritten MMADDR. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: MMADDR does not hold a valid fault address.
MMADDR holds a valid fault address.

fields.name: MLSPERR
fields.text: Memory management fault during floating-point lazy state preservation. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: A memory management fault occurred during lazy state preservation.

fields.name: MSTKE
fields.text: Access violation while stacking on exception entry. The SP is still adjusted, but the stacked context may be wrong, and no address goes to MMADDR. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: Stacking on exception entry caused one or more access violations.

fields.name: MUSTKE
fields.text: Access violation while unstacking on exception return, chained to the handler: the original return stack remains, the SP is not adjusted, no new save is made and no address goes to MMADDR. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: Unstacking on exception return caused one or more access violations.

fields.name: DERR
fields.text: Data access violation; the stacked return PC points at the faulting instruction and the attempted address goes to MMADDR. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: A load or store was attempted where that operation is not allowed.

fields.name: IERR
fields.text: Instruction access violation, raised by any access to an XN region even with the MPU off or absent; the stacked return PC points at the faulting instruction and no address goes to MMADDR. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: An instruction fetch was attempted where execution is not allowed.

fields.name: DBG
fields.text: Reserved for Debug; must be written 0, or the result is unpredictable.

fields.name: FORCED
fields.text: Hard fault produced by escalating a configurable-priority fault that could not be handled, through priority or because it is disabled; the hard fault handler must then read the other fault status registers for the cause. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: A forced hard fault occurred by escalation.

fields.name: VECT
fields.text: Bus fault on a vector table read, always taken by the hard fault handler; the stacked return PC points at the instruction the exception preempted. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: Reading the vector table caused a bus fault.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Address of the location that caused the memory management fault, valid while MFAULTSTAT.MMARV is set.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Address of the location that caused the bus fault, valid while BFAULTSTAT.FAULTADDRV is set.

fields.name: IREGION
fields.text: Count of MPU instruction regions; always reads 0x00. The MPU map is unified and DREGION describes it.

fields.name: DREGION
fields.text: Count of MPU data regions the part supports.

fields.name: SEPARATE
fields.text: Tells whether the MPU has separate instruction and data maps or one unified map.

registers.name: MPUCTRL
registers.title: MPU Control
notes: Privileged access only. With ENABLE and PRIVDEFEN both set, privileged accesses outside enabled regions follow the default memory map and unprivileged ones raise a memory management fault.
Execute Never and Strongly Ordered rules apply to the System Control Space whatever ENABLE holds; with the MPU on, accesses to the System Control Space and the vector table are never blocked.
With ENABLE set, at least one region must be enabled for the system to run unless PRIVDEFEN is set; PRIVDEFEN set with no regions enabled lets only privileged software run.
With ENABLE clear, privileged and unprivileged accesses use the default memory map, as if no MPU were fitted.
Unless HFNMIENA is set, the MPU is off while handling an exception at priority -1 or -2 (hard fault, NMI, or with FAULTMASK set).

fields.name: PRIVDEFEN
fields.text: Lets privileged software fall back on the default memory map outside defined regions, treated as region -1 and outranked by every defined, enabled region; ignored while the MPU is off.

values.text: With the MPU on, no background map: an access outside every enabled region faults.
With the MPU on, privileged accesses outside enabled regions use the default map.

fields.name: HFNMIENA
fields.text: Keeps the MPU active inside the hard fault, NMI and FAULTMASK handlers; setting it with the MPU off gives unpredictable behaviour.

values.text: MPU off in hard fault, NMI and FAULTMASK handlers whatever ENABLE holds.
MPU on in hard fault, NMI and FAULTMASK handlers.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the MPU on; with the MPU off and HFNMIENA set, behaviour is unpredictable.

registers.name: MPUNUMBER
registers.title: MPU Region Number
notes: Privileged access only. Write the region number here before touching MPUBASE or MPUATTR; a write to MPUBASE with VALID set also changes it.

fields.name: NUMBER
fields.text: Picks which of the eight MPU regions MPUBASE and MPUATTR act on.

registers.name: MPUBASE
registers.title: MPU Region Base Address
notes: Privileged access only. The base address must be aligned to the region size (a 64-KB region sits on a 64-KB boundary); a 4-GB region has no ADDR field and starts at 0x0000.0000.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Region base address in bits 31:N, where N = log2 of the region size in bytes; bits (N-1):5 are reserved, so keep their value on a read-modify-write and do not depend on it.

fields.name: VALID
fields.text: On a write, chooses whether REGION also loads MPUNUMBER; reads back as 0.

values.text: MPUNUMBER stays; the base address goes to the region MPUNUMBER names and REGION is ignored.
REGION is copied into MPUNUMBER and the base address goes to that region.

fields.name: REGION
fields.text: Written: the region number to load into MPUNUMBER. Read: the region number now in MPUNUMBER.

notes: Sets coprocessor access rights.

fields.name: CP11
fields.text: Access rights for coprocessor CP11.

values.text: No access; any access raises a NOCP usage fault.
Privileged only; an unprivileged access raises a NOCP fault.

fields.name: ASPEN
fields.text: When 1, executing a floating-point instruction brings the CONTROL register's FRACTV bit into use, so hardware saves FP context on exception entry and restores it on exit. Whether FPCA can be enabled is set by ASPEN together with ACTLR.DISFPCA.

fields.name: LSPEN
fields.text: When 1, floating-point context is preserved lazily and automatically.

fields.name: MONRDY
fields.text: Reads 1 if DebugMonitor was enabled, with priority allowing MON_PEND to be set, at the moment the FP stack frame was reserved.

fields.name: BFRDY
fields.text: Reads 1 if BusFault was enabled, with priority allowing its handler to go pending, at the moment the FP stack frame was reserved.

fields.name: MMRDY
fields.text: Reads 1 if MemManage was enabled, with priority allowing its handler to go pending, at the moment the FP stack frame was reserved.

fields.name: HFRDY
fields.text: Reads 1 if priority allowed the HardFault handler to go pending at the moment the FP stack frame was reserved.

fields.name: THREAD
fields.text: Reads 1 if the processor ran in Thread mode at the moment the FP stack frame was reserved.

fields.name: USER
fields.text: Reads 1 if software ran unprivileged (user level) at the moment the FP stack frame was reserved.

fields.name: LSPACT
fields.text: Reads 1 while lazy preservation is pending: a floating-point stack frame is reserved but the state has not yet been written to it.

registers.name: FPCA
registers.title: Floating-Point Context Address
notes: Holds where the empty floating-point register area of an exception stack frame lies.

fields.name: ADDRESS
fields.text: Address of the reserved, still empty floating-point register area in an exception stack frame.

registers.name: FPDSC
registers.title: Floating-Point Default Status Control
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00000000.
Holds the default values loaded into FPSC.

fields.name: AHP
fields.text: Default for the FPSC AHP bit.

fields.name: DN
fields.text: Default for the FPSC DN bit.

fields.name: FZ
fields.text: Default for the FPSC FZ bit.

fields.name: RMODE
fields.text: Default for the FPSC RMODE rounding-mode field.

registers.name: DID0
registers.title: Device Identification 0
notes: MAJOR and MINOR together give the die and part revision: 0x0/0x0 A0 (part revision 1), 0x0/0x1 A1 (2), 0x0/0x2 A2 (3), 0x0/0x3 A3 (4), 0x1/0x0 B0 (5), 0x1/0x1 B1 (6), 0x1/0x2 B2 (7).

fields.name: VER
fields.text: Format version of DID0; codes other than those listed are reserved.

fields.name: CLASS
fields.text: Product-line design class; together with DID1.PARTNO it names the part. It changes for a new product line, a fab-process change such as a remap or shrink, or when MAJOR and MINOR alone cannot tell parts apart. Other codes are reserved.

fields.name: MAJOR
fields.text: Major die revision: counts changes to the design's base layers; with MINOR it gives the part revision.

fields.name: MINOR
fields.text: Minor die revision: counts metal-layer changes, restarting at 0 whenever MAJOR changes.

values.text: First device, or just after a major revision.

fields.name: VER
fields.text: Format version of DID1; codes other than those listed are reserved.

values.text: First DID1 format, used by Stellaris LM3Snnn parts.

fields.name: FAM
fields.text: Product family of the part; other codes are reserved.

values.text: Tiva C Series and older Stellaris parts: every part numbered TM4C, LM4F or LM3S.

fields.name: PARTNO
fields.text: Part number within the family; the reset value identifies the TM4C1230C3PM.

fields.name: PINCOUNT
fields.text: Pin count of the package; other codes are reserved.

fields.name: TEMP
fields.text: Temperature rating of the part; other codes are reserved.

values.text: Sold in both industrial (-40 to 85 °C) and extended (-40 to 105 °C) versions, told apart by order number.

fields.name: PKG
fields.text: Package type; other codes are reserved.

fields.name: ROHS
fields.text: Reads 1 when the part is RoHS compliant.

fields.name: QUAL
fields.text: Qualification status of the part; other codes are reserved.

registers.name: PBORCTL
registers.title: Brown-Out Reset Control
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00007FFF.
The BOR trip voltages are simulated figures, not yet characterized, and may change.

fields.name: BOR0
fields.text: Chooses what happens when VDD falls below the BOR0 trip point of 3.02 V ±90 mV.

fields.name: BOR1
fields.text: Chooses what happens when VDD falls below the BOR1 trip point of 2.88 V ±90 mV.

fields.name: BOR0RIS
fields.text: Raw status of a VDD drop below BOR0; it can raise an interrupt only while PBORCTL.BOR0 is 0. Cleared by writing 1 to MISC.BOR0MIS.

fields.name: VDDARIS
fields.text: Raw status of the VDDA power-good event; cleared by writing 1 to MISC.VDDAMIS.

values.text: VDDA not at its working voltage.

fields.name: MOSCPUPRIS
fields.text: Raw status of main-oscillator power-up; cleared by writing 1 to MISC.MOSCPUPMIS.

values.text: MOSC start-up time not yet over.
The TMOSC_START time has passed and the MOSC should be at frequency.

fields.name: PLLLRIS
fields.text: Raw status of PLL lock; cleared by writing 1 to MISC.PLLLMIS.

values.text: PLL timer has not reached TREADY.
PLL timer has reached TREADY, long enough for the PLL to lock.

fields.name: MOFRIS
fields.text: Raw status of a main-oscillator failure; cleared by writing 1 to MISC.MOFMIS.

values.text: Main oscillator failed while MOSCCTL.MOSCIM is 1.

fields.name: BOR1RIS
fields.text: Raw status of a VDD drop below BOR1; it can raise an interrupt only while PBORCTL.BOR1 is 0. Cleared by writing 1 to MISC.BOR1MIS.

fields.name: BOR0IM
fields.text: Lets RIS.BOR0RIS reach the interrupt controller.

fields.name: VDDAIM
fields.text: Lets RIS.VDDARIS reach the interrupt controller.

fields.name: MOSCPUPIM
fields.text: Lets RIS.MOSCPUPRIS reach the interrupt controller.

fields.name: PLLLIM
fields.text: Lets RIS.PLLLRIS reach the interrupt controller.

fields.name: MOFIM
fields.text: Lets RIS.MOFRIS reach the interrupt controller.

fields.name: BOR1IM
fields.text: Lets RIS.BOR1RIS reach the interrupt controller.

fields.name: BOR0MIS
fields.text: Masked BOR0 interrupt status; write 1 to clear it and RIS.BOR0RIS.

values.text: Read: no BOR0 condition. Writing 0 does nothing.
Read: an unmasked BOR0 interrupt was raised. Writing 1 clears this bit and RIS.BOR0RIS.

fields.name: VDDAMIS
fields.text: Masked VDDA power-good interrupt status; write 1 to clear it and RIS.VDDARIS.

values.text: Read: VDDA is good. Writing 0 does nothing.
Read: an unmasked interrupt was raised because VDDA fell below its working voltage. Writing 1 clears this bit and RIS.VDDARIS.

fields.name: MOSCPUPMIS
fields.text: Masked MOSC power-up interrupt status; write 1 to clear it and RIS.MOSCPUPRIS.

values.text: Read: the MOSC PLL lock time has not yet passed. Writing 0 does nothing.
Read: an unmasked interrupt was raised once the MOSC PLL lock time passed. Writing 1 clears this bit and RIS.MOSCPUPRIS.

fields.name: PLLLMIS
fields.text: Masked PLL lock interrupt status; write 1 to clear it and RIS.PLLLRIS.

values.text: Read: the PLL lock time has not yet passed. Writing 0 does nothing.
Read: an unmasked interrupt was raised once the PLL lock time passed. Writing 1 clears this bit and RIS.PLLLRIS.

fields.name: MOFMIS
fields.text: Masked main-oscillator failure interrupt status; write 1 to clear it and RIS.MOFRIS.

values.text: Read: main oscillator has not failed. Writing 0 does nothing.
Read: an unmasked interrupt was raised by a main-oscillator failure. Writing 1 clears this bit and RIS.MOFRIS.

fields.name: BOR1MIS
fields.text: Masked BOR1 interrupt status; write 1 to clear it and RIS.BOR1RIS.

values.text: Read: no BOR1 condition. Writing 0 does nothing.
Read: an unmasked BOR1 interrupt was raised. Writing 1 clears this bit and RIS.BOR1RIS.

registers.name: RESC
registers.title: Reset Cause
notes: The bits survive later resets; a power-on reset clears every bit except POR.

fields.name: MOSCFAIL
fields.text: Records a reset caused by main-oscillator failure; write 0 to clear.

values.text: No MOSC-failure reset since the last power-on reset; writing 0 clears the bit.
The MOSC, enabled for clock validation, failed while MOSCCTL.MOSCIM was 0 and caused a reset.

fields.name: WDT1
fields.text: Records a reset caused by Watchdog Timer 1; write 0 to clear.

values.text: No Watchdog Timer 1 reset since the last power-on reset; writing 0 clears the bit.
Watchdog Timer 1 timed out and reset the part.

fields.name: SW
fields.text: Records a software reset; write 0 to clear.

values.text: No software reset since the last power-on reset; writing 0 clears the bit.

fields.name: WDT0
fields.text: Records a reset caused by Watchdog Timer 0; write 0 to clear.

values.text: No Watchdog Timer 0 reset since the last power-on reset; writing 0 clears the bit.
Watchdog Timer 0 timed out and reset the part.

fields.name: BOR
fields.text: Records a brown-out reset from BOR0 or BOR1; write 0 to clear.

values.text: No brown-out reset since the last power-on reset; writing 0 clears the bit.
A BOR0 or BOR1 brown-out reset occurred.

fields.name: POR
fields.text: Records a power-on reset; write 0 to clear.

values.text: No power-on reset recorded; writing 0 clears the bit.

fields.name: EXT
fields.text: Records a reset from the RST pin; write 0 to clear.

values.text: No RST-pin reset since the last power-on reset; writing 0 clears the bit.

registers.name: RCC
registers.title: Run-Mode Clock Configuration
notes: RCC is written before RCC2.

fields.name: ACG
fields.text: Selects which gating registers control peripheral clocks in Sleep and Deep-Sleep; Run mode always uses the RCGCn registers.

values.text: RCGCn registers stay in charge during sleep.
SCGCn in Sleep and DCGCn in Deep-Sleep, so unused peripherals draw less power.

fields.name: SYSDIV
fields.text: Divisor applied to the PLL output or the oscillator, as BYPASS selects, to make the system clock. With the PLL in use, a value under DC1.MINSYSDIV is replaced by MINSYSDIV; without the PLL, smaller values are allowed.

fields.name: USESYSDIV
fields.text: Turns on the system clock divider.

values.text: System clock comes through the divider, which is always used when the PLL is the source. With RCC2.USERCC2 set, RCC2.SYSDIV2 is the divisor instead of SYSDIV.

fields.name: PWRDN
fields.text: Powers the PLL down.

values.text: PLL off; another clock source must be running and BYPASS set before this bit is set.

fields.name: BYPASS
fields.text: Chooses whether the system clock comes from the PLL or straight from the OSC source. The ADC needs its clock from the PLL or a direct 16 MHz source to work.

fields.name: XTAL
fields.text: Frequency of the crystal on the main oscillator, as a code.

columns: Crystal Frequency (MHz) Not Using the PLL

fields.name: OSCSRC
fields.text: Input chosen for OSC; RCC2 offers further sources.

values.text: PIOSC, the precision internal oscillator; reset default.

fields.name: MOSCDIS
fields.text: Turns the main oscillator off.

registers.name: GPIOHBCTL
registers.title: GPIO High-Performance Bus Control
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00007E00.
A GPIO port is reached over one bus at a time; a port moved to AHB answers at its AHB address range, and AHB gives faster back-to-back access than APB.

fields.name: PORTG
fields.text: Bus through which Port G is reached.

fields.name: PORTF
fields.text: Bus through which Port F is reached.

fields.name: PORTE
fields.text: Bus through which Port E is reached.

fields.name: PORTD
fields.text: Bus through which Port D is reached.

fields.name: PORTC
fields.text: Bus through which Port C is reached.

fields.name: PORTB
fields.text: Bus through which Port B is reached.

fields.name: PORTA
fields.text: Bus through which Port A is reached.

registers.name: RCC2
registers.title: Run-Mode Clock Configuration 2
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x07C06810.
RCC is written before RCC2.
While USERCC2 is 1, SYSDIV2, PWRDN2, BYPASS2 and OSCSRC2 take the place of RCC.SYSDIV, PWRDN, BYPASS and OSCSRC; each sits at the same low bit, and SYSDIV2 and OSCSRC2 are wider.

fields.name: USERCC2
fields.text: Makes RCC2 take over from RCC.

values.text: RCC fields in force; RCC2 ignored.
RCC2 fields override the matching RCC fields.

fields.name: DIV400
fields.text: With SYSDIV2LSB, widens the choice of system clock frequencies by dividing the PLL at 400 MHz instead of 200 MHz.

values.text: SYSDIV2 divides the 200 MHz pre-divided PLL output.
SYSDIV2LSB joins SYSDIV2 as a 7-bit divisor of the 400 MHz PLL output.

fields.name: SYSDIV2
fields.text: Divisor applied to the PLL output or the oscillator, as BYPASS2 selects, to make the system clock; in force when both RCC.USESYSDIV and USERCC2 are set.

fields.name: SYSDIV2LSB
fields.text: Extra low bit of SYSDIV2, used only while DIV400 is set and writable only then.

fields.name: PWRDN2
fields.text: Powers the PLL down.

fields.name: BYPASS2
fields.text: Chooses whether the system clock comes from the PLL or straight from the OSC source. The ADC needs its clock from the PLL or a direct 16 MHz source to work.

fields.name: OSCSRC2
fields.text: Input chosen for OSC.

fields.name: NOXTAL
fields.text: Tells the part whether anything is wired to OSC0 and OSC1.

values.text: Keep 0 whenever OSC0/OSC1 have a crystal or oscillator attached, even if the MOSC is unused or off.
Set when no crystal or external oscillator is connected to OSC0/OSC1, to save power.

fields.name: MOSCIM
fields.text: Chooses the response to a main-oscillator failure; in either case the clock source switches to the PIOSC by itself.

values.text: MOSC failure reset, restarting into the NMI handler.

fields.name: CVAL
fields.text: Turns on the circuit that watches the main oscillator.

fields.name: DSDIVORIDE
fields.text: Six-bit system clock divider used in Deep-Sleep in place of RCC.SYSDIV or RCC2.SYSDIV2, applied to the clock DSOSCSRC selects; entering Deep-Sleep with the PLL running turns the PLL off.

fields.name: DSOSCSRC
fields.text: Clock source used in Deep-Sleep.

values.text: MOSC; it must also be the Run-mode source in RCC. If the PIOSC is the PLL's reference, the PIOSC is used in Deep-Sleep instead.

fields.name: PIOSCPD
fields.text: Asks for the PIOSC to be off in Deep-Sleep; works only when SYSPROP.PIOSCPDE is 1. If an enabled peripheral needs the PIOSC it is still turned off and SDPMST.PPDW warns; if it cannot be turned off, SDPMST.PPDERR reports it.

fields.name: PIOSCPDE
fields.text: Shows whether DSLPCLKCFG.PIOSCPD can turn the PIOSC off in Deep-Sleep.

values.text: PIOSCPD can power the PIOSC down in Deep-Sleep.

fields.name: SRAMSM
fields.text: Shows whether SRAMPM in SLPPWRCFG and DSLPPWRCFG can select SRAM standby in Sleep or Deep-Sleep.

values.text: SRAMPM can put the SRAM in standby during Sleep or Deep-Sleep.

fields.name: SRAMLPM
fields.text: Shows whether SRAMPM in SLPPWRCFG and DSLPPWRCFG can select SRAM low-power mode in Sleep or Deep-Sleep.

values.text: SRAMPM can put the SRAM in low-power mode during Sleep or Deep-Sleep.

fields.name: FLASHLPM
fields.text: Shows whether FLASHPM in SLPPWRCFG and DSLPPWRCFG can select flash low-power mode in Sleep or Deep-Sleep.

values.text: FLASHPM can put the flash in low-power mode during Sleep or Deep-Sleep.

fields.name: FPU
fields.text: Shows whether the Cortex-M4 core has its FPU.

fields.name: UTEN
fields.text: Chooses which trim value an update loads into the PIOSC.

fields.name: UPDATE
fields.text: Write 1 to load the PIOSC trim, chosen by UTEN; clears itself when done.

values.text: Load the trim value, from UT when UTEN is set.

fields.name: UT
fields.text: User trim value that an update can load into the PIOSC.

registers.name: PLLFREQ0
registers.title: PLL Frequency 0
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00000032.
PLL frequency = XTAL frequency x MDIV / ((Q + 1) x (N + 1)), where MDIV = MINT + MFRAC / 1024; Q and N are held in PLLFREQ1.

fields.name: MFRAC
fields.text: Fractional part of the PLL multiplier M.

fields.name: MINT
fields.text: Integer part of the PLL multiplier M.

fields.name: Q
fields.text: PLL Q value.

fields.name: N
fields.text: PLL N value.

fields.name: LOCK
fields.text: Shows whether the PLL is powered and locked.

values.text: PLL off or not yet locked.

fields.name: FLASHPM
fields.text: Power mode of the flash while the part is in Sleep.

values.text: Active: flash stays fully powered; quickest into and out of Sleep, highest Sleep current.
Low power: lowest current, slower to leave Sleep.

fields.name: SRAMPM
fields.text: Power mode of the on-chip SRAM during low-power modes.

values.text: Active: SRAM stays fully powered; quickest into and out of Sleep, highest Sleep current.
Low power: slowest into and out of Sleep, lowest Sleep current.

fields.name: FLASHPM
fields.text: Power mode of the flash while the part is in Deep-Sleep.

values.text: Active: flash stays fully powered; quickest into and out of Deep-Sleep, highest Deep-Sleep current.
Low power: lowest current, slower to leave Deep-Sleep.

fields.name: SRAMPM
fields.text: Power mode of the on-chip SRAM while the part is in Deep-Sleep.

values.text: Active: SRAM stays fully powered; quickest into and out of Deep-Sleep, highest Deep-Sleep current.
Low power: slowest into and out of Deep-Sleep, lowest Deep-Sleep current.

registers.name: LDOSPCTL
registers.title: LDO Sleep Power Control
notes: A write to VLDO leaves the LDO output unchanged whatever VADJEN holds; the output stays at its factory value.
LDO 1.2 V allows a system clock up to 80 MHz, 0.9 V up to 20 MHz; the PIOSC runs at 16 MHz at both.
If a debugger was attached at any point after the most recent power-on reset, the LDO keeps its voltage in Sleep and Deep-Sleep.
Leaving Sleep or Deep-Sleep takes 4 us longer when the LDO voltage has been adjusted.

fields.name: VADJEN
fields.text: Lets VLDO set the LDO output voltage in Sleep.

values.text: Factory default LDO voltage in Sleep; VLDO ignored.
LDO voltage in Sleep set by VLDO.

fields.name: VLDO
fields.text: LDO output voltage code, used only while VADJEN is 1. A setting at or below the 1.2 V default is recommended for the lowest Sleep power.

fields.name: WITHPLL
fields.text: Suggested LDOSPCTL.VLDO code when the PLL is used: the lowest recommended LDO voltage for the PLL at its maximum specified frequency.

fields.name: NOPLL
fields.text: Suggested LDOSPCTL.VLDO code when the PLL is not used: the lowest recommended LDO voltage without the PLL.

registers.name: LDODPCTL
registers.title: LDO Deep-Sleep Power Control
notes: Set up in Run mode, before Deep-Sleep is entered.
A write to VLDO leaves the LDO output unchanged whatever VADJEN holds; the output stays at its factory value.
LDO 1.2 V allows a system clock up to 80 MHz, 0.9 V up to 20 MHz; the PIOSC runs at 16 MHz at both.
If a debugger was attached at any point after the most recent power-on reset, the LDO keeps its voltage in Sleep and Deep-Sleep.
Leaving Sleep or Deep-Sleep takes 4 us longer when the LDO voltage has been adjusted.

fields.name: VADJEN
fields.text: Lets VLDO set the LDO output voltage in Deep-Sleep.

values.text: Factory default LDO voltage in Deep-Sleep; VLDO ignored.
LDO voltage in Deep-Sleep set by VLDO.

fields.name: VLDO
fields.text: LDO output voltage code, used only while VADJEN is 1. The 0.90 V default is recommended for the lowest Deep-Sleep power.

fields.name: NOPLL
fields.text: Suggested LDODPCTL.VLDO code without the PLL: the lowest recommended LDO voltage when running from the system clock.

fields.name: 30KHZ
fields.text: Suggested LDODPCTL.VLDO code without the PLL: the lowest recommended LDO voltage when running from the low-frequency internal oscillator.

registers.name: SDPMST
registers.title: Sleep / Deep-Sleep Power Mode Status
notes: Written with the error-check results at the start of each Dynamic Power Management event request and overwritten by the next; nothing clears the bits and none raises an interrupt.
LDOUA, FLASHLP, LOWPWR and PRACT show live state rather than recorded events.

fields.name: LDOUA
fields.text: Shows whether the LDO voltage is being changed.

fields.name: FLASHLP
fields.text: Shows whether the flash is in its low-power state.

values.text: Flash in the low-power state set in SLPPWRCFG or DSLPPWRCFG.

fields.name: LOWPWR
fields.text: Shows whether the part is in Sleep or Deep-Sleep.

values.text: In Sleep or Deep-Sleep, waiting for an interrupt or powering back up; not affected by the flash or SRAM power state.

fields.name: PRACT
fields.text: Shows whether a low-power request is active.

values.text: In Deep-Sleep, or in Sleep with a SLPPWRCFG request active to lower SRAM and/or flash power.

fields.name: PPDW
fields.text: Warning that the PIOSC was turned off in Deep-Sleep while a peripheral needed it.

values.text: DSLPCLKCFG.PIOSCPD asked for the PIOSC off in Deep-Sleep while a peripheral needs it active; the PIOSC is turned off anyway.

fields.name: LMAXERR
fields.text: Error: a VLDO setting asked for an LDO voltage above the allowed maximum.

values.text: VLDO in LDOSPCTL or LDODPCTL asked for more than the maximum; the LDO goes to its factory default.

fields.name: LSMINERR
fields.text: Error: LDOSPCTL.VLDO asked for an LDO voltage below the allowed minimum.

values.text: LDOSPCTL.VLDO below the minimum; the LDO voltage is left as is on entering Sleep.

fields.name: LDMINERR
fields.text: Error: LDODPCTL.VLDO asked for an LDO voltage below the allowed minimum.

values.text: LDODPCTL.VLDO below the minimum; the LDO voltage is left as is on entering Deep-Sleep.

fields.name: PPDERR
fields.text: Error: the PIOSC could not be turned off in Deep-Sleep as asked.

values.text: A PIOSC power-down for Deep-Sleep was asked for but is not possible; the PIOSC stays on in Deep-Sleep.

fields.name: FPDERR
fields.text: Error: FLASHPM asked for a flash power mode that is not available.

values.text: FLASHPM in SLPPWRCFG or DSLPPWRCFG holds a flash power mode this part lacks.

fields.name: SPDERR
fields.text: Error: SRAMPM asked for an SRAM power mode that is not available.

values.text: SRAMPM in SLPPWRCFG or DSLPPWRCFG holds an SRAM power mode this part lacks.

registers.name: FMPRE0

notes: Covers flash 0 to 64 KB. Loaded at power-on reset; other resets leave it alone. Factory value is 1 in every implemented block, giving open access.
Bits can only go from 1 to 0. A cleared bit becomes permanent once committed; uncommitted, a power-on reset brings it back.

fields.name: READ_ENABLE
fields.text: One bit per 2 KB flash block setting it read-only; combines with FMPPE0 into the block's protection policy.

registers.name: FMPPE0

notes: Covers flash 0 to 64 KB. Loaded at power-on reset; other resets leave it alone. Factory value is 1 in every implemented block, giving open access.

fields.name: PROG_ENABLE
fields.text: One bit per 2 KB flash block setting it execute-only; combines with FMPRE0 into the block's protection policy.

fields.name: PORT

fields.name: PIN

fields.name: POL
fields.text: Level on the boot pin that starts the ROM boot loader at reset: 1 high, 0 low.

fields.name: EN
fields.text: At 0, a GPIO pin can start the ROM boot loader at reset. At 1, the word at 0x0000.0004 is checked: if it is not 0xFFFF.FFFF the core runs from flash, otherwise from ROM.

fields.name: KEY

values.text: WRKEY is 0x71D5; FMC/FMC2 writes with 0xA442 are ignored.

fields.name: FPIOCRIS

fields.name: FPDZCRIS

SYSEXCRIS.FPIXCRIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: FPOFCIM
fields.text: Mask for the floating-point overflow exception interrupt.

values.text: FPOFCRIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
SYSEXCRIS.FPOFCRIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: FPUFCIM

values.text: FPUFCRIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
SYSEXCRIS.FPUFCRIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: FPIOCIM

values.text: FPIOCRIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
SYSEXCRIS.FPIOCRIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: FPDZCIM

values.text: FPDZCRIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
SYSEXCRIS.FPDZCRIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: FPIDCIM

values.text: FPIDCRIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
SYSEXCRIS.FPIDCRIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: FPIXCMIS
fields.text: Masked status of the floating-point inexact exception interrupt; a 1 written to SYSEXCIC.FPIXCIC clears it.

values.text: No interrupt, or the interrupt is masked.
An unmasked interrupt was raised by an inexact exception.

fields.name: FPOFCMIS
fields.text: Masked status of the floating-point overflow exception interrupt; a 1 written to SYSEXCIC.FPOFCIC clears it.

values.text: No interrupt, or the interrupt is masked.
An unmasked interrupt was raised by an overflow exception.

fields.name: FPUFCMIS
fields.text: Masked status of the floating-point underflow exception interrupt; a 1 written to SYSEXCIC.FPUFCIC clears it.

values.text: No interrupt, or the interrupt is masked.
An unmasked interrupt was raised by an underflow exception.

fields.name: FPIOCMIS

values.text: No interrupt, or the interrupt is masked.
An unmasked interrupt was raised by an invalid operation exception.

fields.name: FPDZCMIS

values.text: No interrupt, or the interrupt is masked.
An unmasked interrupt was raised by a divide by 0 exception.

fields.name: FPIDCMIS

values.text: No interrupt, or the interrupt is masked.

fields.name: OFFSET
fields.text: Flash address offset the operation acts on; the non-volatile registers take their own values here.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Word to be written by the write operation.

fields.name: WRKEY
fields.text: Write key guarding against stray Flash writes: a Flash write happens only when 0xA442 or 0x71D5 is written here, which of the two set by BOOTCFG.KEY. FMC writes with any other key are dropped; reads give 0.

fields.name: COMT
fields.text: Commits a write to a Flash-resident register and shows whether that commit is still running.

values.text: Writing 0 does nothing; reading 0 means the last commit has finished.
Writing 1 commits the value to the Flash-resident register; reading 1 means the last commit is still running.

fields.name: MERASE
fields.text: Mass-erases the Flash main memory and shows whether that erase is still running.

values.text: Writing 0 does nothing; reading 0 means the last mass erase has finished.
Writing 1 erases the Flash main memory; reading 1 means the last mass erase is still running.

fields.name: ERASE
fields.text: Erases one Flash page and shows whether that erase is still running.

values.text: Writing 0 does nothing; reading 0 means the last page erase has finished.
Writing 1 erases the page at the FMA address; reading 1 means the last page erase is still running.

fields.name: WRITE
fields.text: Writes one word into Flash and shows whether that write is still running.

values.text: Writing 0 does nothing; reading 0 means the last write has finished.
Writing 1 stores the FMD word at the FMA address; reading 1 means the write is still running.

fields.name: PROGRIS
fields.text: Raw status of the program verify error interrupt; a 1 written to FCMISC.PROGMISC clears it.

values.text: Interrupt pending: a PROGRAM operation failed its verify; with the write buffer in use, software has to check the affected words to find the failing one.

fields.name: ERRIS
fields.text: Raw status of the erase verify error interrupt; a 1 written to FCMISC.ERMISC clears it.

values.text: Interrupt pending: an ERASE operation failed its verify; with the write buffer in use, software has to check the affected words to find the failing one.

fields.name: INVDRIS
fields.text: Raw status of the invalid data interrupt; a 1 written to FCMISC.INVMISC clears it.

values.text: Interrupt pending: a bit already programmed to 0 was asked to be programmed to 1.

fields.name: VOLTRIS
fields.text: Raw status of the pump voltage interrupt; a 1 written to FCMISC.VOLTMISC clears it.

values.text: Interrupt pending: the pump's regulated voltage left its specified range during a Flash operation, and the operation was stopped.

fields.name: ERIS
fields.text: Raw status of EEPROM operations; a 1 written to FCMISC.EMISC clears it.

fields.name: PRIS
fields.text: Raw status of program and erase cycles started by FMC or FMC2 bits; goes to the interrupt controller when FCIM.PMASK is set, and a 1 written to FCMISC.PMISC clears it.

values.text: The program or erase cycle is not finished.
The program or erase cycle is finished.

fields.name: ARIS
fields.text: Raw status of improper program or erase attempts; goes to the interrupt controller when FCIM.AMASK is set, and a 1 written to FCMISC.AMISC clears it.

values.text: No attempt to program or erase Flash against its protection.
A program or erase was tried on a Flash block whose FMPPEn protection forbids it.

fields.name: PROGMASK
fields.text: Passes the program verify error raw interrupt (PROGRIS) on to the interrupt controller, or not.

values.text: PROGRIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
PROGRIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: ERMASK
fields.text: Passes the erase verify error raw interrupt (ERRIS) on to the interrupt controller, or not.

values.text: ERRIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
ERRIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: INVDMASK
fields.text: Passes the invalid data raw interrupt (INVDRIS) on to the interrupt controller, or not.

values.text: INVDRIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
INVDRIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: VOLTMASK
fields.text: Passes the pump voltage raw interrupt (VOLTRIS) on to the interrupt controller, or not.

values.text: VOLTRIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
VOLTRIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: EMASK
fields.text: Passes the EEPROM raw interrupt (ERIS) on to the interrupt controller, or not.

values.text: ERIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
ERIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: PMASK
fields.text: Passes the programming raw interrupt (PRIS) on to the interrupt controller, or not.

values.text: PRIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
PRIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: AMASK
fields.text: Passes the access raw interrupt (ARIS) on to the interrupt controller, or not.

values.text: ARIS is kept from the interrupt controller.
ARIS set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

registers.name: FCMISC
registers.title: Flash Controller Masked Interrupt Status and Clear

fields.name: PROGMISC
fields.text: Masked status of the program verify error interrupt; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Reads 0 when no interrupt has happened; writing 0 does nothing.
Reads 1 when an unmasked interrupt was raised; writing 1 clears PROGMISC and FCRIS.PROGRIS.

fields.name: ERMISC
fields.text: Masked status of the erase verify error interrupt; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Reads 0 when no interrupt has happened; writing 0 does nothing.
Reads 1 when an unmasked interrupt was raised; writing 1 clears ERMISC and FCRIS.ERRIS.

fields.name: INVDMISC
fields.text: Masked status of the invalid data interrupt; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Reads 0 when no interrupt has happened; writing 0 does nothing.
Reads 1 when an unmasked interrupt was raised; writing 1 clears INVDMISC and FCRIS.INVDRIS.

fields.name: VOLTMISC
fields.text: Masked status of the pump voltage interrupt; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Reads 0 when no interrupt has happened; writing 0 does nothing.
Reads 1 when an unmasked interrupt was raised; writing 1 clears VOLTMISC and FCRIS.VOLTRIS.

fields.name: EMISC
fields.text: Masked status of the EEPROM interrupt; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Reads 0 when no interrupt has happened; writing 0 does nothing.
Reads 1 when an unmasked interrupt was raised; writing 1 clears EMISC and FCRIS.ERIS.

fields.name: PMISC
fields.text: Masked status of the programming interrupt; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Reads 0 when no program-cycle-complete interrupt has happened; writing 0 does nothing.
Reads 1 when an unmasked interrupt was raised because a program cycle finished; writing 1 clears PMISC and FCRIS.PRIS.

fields.name: AMISC
fields.text: Masked status of the access interrupt; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Reads 0 when no improper access has happened; writing 0 does nothing.
Reads 1 when an unmasked interrupt was raised because a program or erase was tried on a Flash block whose FMPPEn protection forbids it; writing 1 clears AMISC and FCRIS.ARIS.

fields.name: WRKEY
fields.text: Write key guarding against stray Flash writes: a Flash write happens only when 0xA442 or 0x71D5 is written here, which of the two set by BOOTCFG.KEY. FMC2 writes with any other key are dropped; reads give 0.

fields.name: WRBUF
fields.text: Starts a buffered write to Flash and shows whether it is still running.

values.text: Writing 0 does nothing; reading 0 means the last buffered write has finished.
Writing 1 stores the FWBn data at the FMA address; reading 1 means the last buffered write is still running.

fields.name: FWB[n]
fields.text: One bit per write-buffer register: bit 0 is FWB0 at offset 0x100, bit 31 is FWB31 at offset 0x13C.

values.text: That FWBn holds no new data to write.
That FWBn was written since the last buffer write and goes to Flash on the next one.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Word to be stored in Flash by a buffered write.

fields.name: SIZE
fields.text: Size of the on-chip Flash.

fields.name: SIZE
fields.text: Size of the on-chip SRAM.

fields.name: SAFERTOS
fields.text: Shows whether SafeRTOS is in the on-chip ROM.

fields.name: BLKCNT
fields.text: How many 16-word blocks the EEPROM has.

fields.name: WORDCNT
fields.text: How many 32-bit words the EEPROM has.

fields.name: BLOCK
fields.text: Picks the EEPROM block that following accesses use: the read-write registers act on it with EEOFFSET choosing the word, and the protection and unlock registers apply to it. The largest allowed value follows the block count in EESIZE; writing a larger value, or a locked block, sets this field to 0.

fields.name: OFFSET
fields.text: Word offset within the EEBLOCK block that EERDWR and EERDWRINC act on; EERDWRINC steps it up by one, wrapping from 15 to 0 inside the block.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: Reads give the word at EEOFFSET; a write stores its data at that word and starts the write. Reads that protection forbids return all 1s; writes it forbids fail, with the failure shown in EEDONE.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: Reads give the word at EEOFFSET; a write stores its data at that word and starts the write. Reads that protection forbids return all 1s; writes it forbids fail, with the failure shown in EEDONE. Either way EEOFFSET.OFFSET then goes up by 1, wrapping after the last word.

fields.name: WRBUSY
fields.text: Write busy error.

values.text: The EEPROM was accessed while a write was running.

fields.name: NOPERM
fields.text: Write-without-permission error.

values.text: A write lacked permission: the block is locked, the write breaks the access protection, or a password was written when one is already set.

fields.name: WKCOPY
fields.text: Shows the EEPROM busy with a copy.

values.text: A write is running and waits on the EEPROM copying to or from the copy buffer.

fields.name: WKERASE
fields.text: Shows the EEPROM busy with an erase.

values.text: A write is running, and the original block is being erased now that its copy is made.

fields.name: WORKING
fields.text: Shows the EEPROM busy.

fields.name: PRETRY
fields.text: Shows that programming has to be retried.

values.text: Programming from a copy, in either direction, did not finish; setting START restarts it.

fields.name: ERETRY
fields.text: Shows that an erase has to be retried.

values.text: An erase did not finish; setting START restarts it. When the failed erase was of a main buffer, the copy follows once the erase succeeds.

fields.name: EREQ
fields.text: Shows that the copy buffer needs erasing.

values.text: The copy buffer has space left.
The copy buffer has to be erased.

fields.name: START
fields.text: Writing 1 starts error recovery when PRETRY or ERETRY is set; with both clear it starts a copy-buffer erase when EREQ is set; with nothing else set it is ignored. EEDONE.WORKING is set while the operation runs and clears at the end, and EEINT can raise an interrupt then. Setting it while an operation runs is ignored; it clears itself when the operation finishes.

fields.name: UNLOCK
fields.text: The EEPROM is locked when the EEBLOCK block, or block 0, has a password. Writing the password here unlocks it until it is locked again or the next reset; writing 0xFFFF.FFFF locks it again.

fields.name: ACC
fields.text: Limits access to the block to supervisor code; set on block 0, it limits the whole EEPROM that way.

values.text: User and supervisor code may both access the block.
Only supervisor code may access the block; μDMA and debug are kept out too.

fields.name: PROT
fields.text: Sets what is needed to read and write the EEBLOCK block, or every block when block 0 is chosen.

values.text: Default. Without a password the block reads and writes freely; with one it reads freely and writes only when unlocked.
With a password the block reads and writes only when unlocked; without one this setting means nothing.
Without a password the block reads but never writes; with one it reads only when unlocked and never writes.

fields.name: PASS
fields.text: Reads 0x1 when the block has a password and 0x0 when not. Writing while it reads 0x0 sets the password; writing while it reads 0x1 is ignored and sets EEDONE.NOPERM.

fields.name: PASS
fields.text: Reads 0x1 when the block has a password and 0x0 when not. Writing while it reads 0x0 sets the password; writing while it reads 0x1 is ignored and sets EEDONE.NOPERM.

fields.name: PASS
fields.text: Reads 0x1 when the block has a password and 0x0 when not. Writing while it reads 0x0 sets the password; writing while it reads 0x1 is ignored and sets EEDONE.NOPERM.

fields.name: INT
fields.text: Interrupt enable for EEPROM completion.

values.text: An interrupt is raised when EEDONE goes from 1 to 0 or an error happens; EEDONE reports on writes to an offset word and to the password and protection bits.

fields.name: Hn
fields.text: One bit per block from block 1 up, hiding that block.

values.text: The block numbered by this bit is hidden: it cannot be accessed and EEBLOCK cannot be set to it; an attempt to do so clears EEBLOCK. A set bit cannot be cleared by a write.

fields.name: KEY
fields.text: Erase key: ME acts only when 0xE37B is written here.

fields.name: ME
fields.text: Mass-erases the EEPROM.

values.text: Writing 1 mass-erases the EEPROM; it keeps reading 1 until the erase is done.

fields.name: SIZE
fields.text: Size of the EEPROM (2-KB EEPROM size).

registers.name: DMASRCENDP
registers.title: DMA Channel Source Address End Pointer

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Last address of the transfer source, included. When the source address is fixed (DMACHCTL.SRCINC is 0x3), it points straight at the source, a peripheral data register for example.

registers.name: DMADSTENDP
registers.title: DMA Channel Destination Address End Pointer

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Last address of the transfer destination, included. When the destination address is fixed (DMACHCTL.DSTINC is 0x3), it points straight at the destination, a peripheral data register for example.

fields.name: DSTINC
fields.text: Step the destination address takes per item; it must be no smaller than DSTSIZE.

values.text: No increment: stays at the channel's DMADSTENDP.

fields.name: DSTSIZE
fields.text: Size of each destination item; must match SRCSIZE.

fields.name: SRCINC
fields.text: Step the source address takes per item; it must be no smaller than SRCSIZE.

values.text: No increment: stays at the channel's DMASRCENDP.

fields.name: SRCSIZE
fields.text: Size of each source item; must match DSTSIZE.

fields.name: ARBSIZE
fields.text: How many transfers run before the μDMA controller arbitrates again, as a power of 2.

values.text: 1024 transfers: no arbitration during the transfer, 1024 being the largest transfer size.

fields.name: XFERSIZE
fields.text: Number of items to move, less one (0 moves 1 item, 1023 the most, moves 1024). It counts items, not bytes: at 32-bit size it counts words. The controller rewrites it just before each arbitration, so it holds the items still left in the cycle.

fields.name: NXTUSEBURST
fields.text: Sets whether the Useburst SET[n] bit is set by itself for the final transfer of a peripheral scatter-gather run. Without it, a final transfer with fewer items left than the arbitration size finishes with single transfers; with it set, it finishes with a burst.

fields.name: XFERMODE
fields.text: Operating mode of the μDMA cycle. The word sits in system RAM and has no reset value, so this field is to be set to 0 before the channel is enabled.

fields.name: DMACHANS
fields.text: Number of μDMA channels the controller is set up to use, less one; 0x1F means 32 channels.

fields.name: STATE
fields.text: Present state of the controller's control state machine.

values.text: Waiting for the μDMA request to clear.

fields.name: MASTEN
fields.text: Shows whether the μDMA controller is enabled.

fields.name: MASTEN
fields.text: Turns the μDMA controller on or off.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Base address of the channel control table; it must sit on a 1024-byte boundary.

registers.name: DMAALTBASE
registers.title: DMA Alternate Channel Control Base Pointer

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Address where the alternate channel control structures start.

fields.name: WAITREQ[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel, bit 0 for channel 0, showing whether that channel is waiting on a request.

fields.name: SWREQ[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel, bit 0 for channel 0; writing 1 issues a software request for that channel, and the bit clears itself once the request is done.

values.text: Issue a software request for that channel.

fields.name: SET[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel, bit 0 for channel 0; set, the channel ignores single requests and takes only burst requests. The controller clears it after the final transfer when the data is a whole number of bursts, or when fewer items remain than the burst size so the rest go by single requests; setting DMAUSEBURSTCLR.CLR[n] also clears it.

values.text: Channel answers single and burst requests.

fields.name: CLR[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel; writing 1 clears DMAUSEBURSTSET.SET[n].

values.text: Clears DMAUSEBURSTSET.SET[n], so the channel answers single and burst requests.

fields.name: SET[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel, bit 0 for channel 0; set, the channel's peripheral can no longer request μDMA transfers. Only setting DMAREQMASKCLR.CLR[n] clears it.

values.text: The channel's peripheral may request μDMA transfers.
The channel's peripheral cannot request μDMA transfers; the channel can serve software-started transfers.

fields.name: CLR[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel; writing 1 clears DMAREQMASKSET.SET[n].

values.text: Clears DMAREQMASKSET.SET[n], letting the channel's peripheral request μDMA transfers.

fields.name: SET[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel, bit 0 for channel 0; writing 1 enables the channel and a read gives its enable state. It clears only through DMAENACLR.CLR[n] or at the end of a μDMA transfer.

fields.name: CLR[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel; writing 1 clears DMAENASET.SET[n]. The controller also disables a channel itself when its μDMA cycle completes.

values.text: Clears DMAENASET.SET[n], disabling the channel for μDMA transfers.

fields.name: SET[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel, bit 0 for channel 0; set, the channel uses its alternate control data structure. Only setting DMAALTCLR.CLR[n] clears it; in Ping-Pong and Scatter-Gather cycles the controller sets it on its own.

values.text: Channel uses the primary control structure.
Channel uses the alternate control structure.

fields.name: CLR[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel; writing 1 clears DMAALTSET.SET[n]. In Ping-Pong and Scatter-Gather cycles the controller sets DMAALTSET bits on its own.

values.text: Clears DMAALTSET.SET[n], returning the channel to the primary control structure.

fields.name: SET[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel, bit 0 for channel 0; set, the channel runs at high priority. Only setting DMAPRIOCLR.CLR[n] clears it.

fields.name: CLR[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel; writing 1 clears DMAPRIOSET.SET[n].

values.text: Clears DMAPRIOSET.SET[n], returning the channel to default priority.

fields.name: ERRCLR
fields.text: Flags a μDMA bus error; writing 1 clears it.

registers.name: DMACHASGN
registers.title: DMA Channel Assignment
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00000000.

fields.name: CHASGN[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel picking its primary or secondary channel assignment.

fields.name: CHIS[n]
fields.text: One bit per channel, set when that channel raises a completion interrupt; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Channel has not raised an interrupt.

fields.text: Peripheral ID byte that software can read to detect this peripheral.

fields.text: Peripheral ID byte that software can read to detect this peripheral.

fields.text: Peripheral ID byte that software can read to detect this peripheral.

fields.text: PrimeCell ID byte, part of a standard ID scheme common across peripherals.

fields.text: PrimeCell ID byte, part of a standard ID scheme common across peripherals.

fields.text: PrimeCell ID byte, part of a standard ID scheme common across peripherals.

fields.text: PrimeCell ID byte, part of a standard ID scheme common across peripherals.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Port pin data, seen at 256 addresses: address bits [9:2] mask each access, so a read returns only the unmasked bits (masked bits read 0) and a write changes only unmasked bits of pins set as outputs. Output pins read back the last value written; input pins read the pin level.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Direction of each pin, one bit per pin.

fields.name: IS
fields.text: Selects edge or level detection for each pin's interrupt.

fields.name: IBE
fields.text: With GPIOIS set for edges, a set bit makes the pin interrupt on both edges whatever GPIOIEV holds.

fields.name: IEV
fields.text: Selects which edge or level of each pin raises an interrupt, with GPIOIS choosing edge or level.

fields.name: IME
fields.text: Per-pin enable for passing the pin's interrupt to the interrupt controller.

fields.name: RIS
fields.text: Per-pin interrupt flag before masking. An edge flag is cleared by a 1 written to the pin's GPIOICR bit; a level flag clears when the input leaves its interrupting level.

fields.name: MIS
fields.text: Per-pin interrupt flag after masking by GPIOIM. An edge flag is cleared by a 1 written to the pin's GPIOICR bit; a level flag clears when the input leaves its interrupting level.

fields.name: IC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear a pin's edge interrupt in GPIORIS and GPIOMIS; it has no effect on level interrupts, and a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: AFSEL
fields.text: Gives each pin to a peripheral or keeps it as a GPIO; GPIOPCTL picks which peripheral. Resets to 0 on ports without special-consideration pins. Writes to the JTAG/SWD and NMI pins' bits take effect only once GPIOLOCK is unlocked and the GPIOCR bit is set.

values.text: GPIO, run by the GPIO registers.
Peripheral signal, run by the alternate function.

fields.name: DRV2
fields.text: Sets 2-mA drive on each pin. Setting a bit clears the pin's bits in GPIODR4R and GPIODR8R, and setting either of those clears this bit. A write takes effect on the second clock after it through the APB aperture, on the next clock through AHB.

values.text: Drive set by GPIODR4R or GPIODR8R.

fields.name: DRV4
fields.text: Sets 4-mA drive on each pin. Setting a bit clears the pin's bits in GPIODR2R and GPIODR8R, and setting either of those clears this bit. A write takes effect on the second clock after it through the APB aperture, on the next clock through AHB.

values.text: Drive set by GPIODR2R or GPIODR8R.

fields.name: DRV8
fields.text: Sets 8-mA drive on each pin, also the high-current setting. Setting a bit clears the pin's bits in GPIODR2R and GPIODR4R, and setting either of those clears this bit. A write takes effect on the second clock after it through the APB aperture, on the next clock through AHB.

values.text: Drive set by GPIODR2R or GPIODR4R.

fields.name: ODE
fields.text: Makes each pin's output open drain; it has no effect while the pin is an input.

fields.name: PUE
fields.text: Turns on each pin's weak pull-up. Setting a bit clears the pin's GPIOPDR bit, and setting the GPIOPDR bit clears this one. A write takes effect on the second clock after it through the APB aperture, on the next clock through AHB. Bits whose GPIOCR bit is 0 cannot be written.

fields.name: PDE
fields.text: Turns on each pin's weak pull-down. Setting a bit clears the pin's GPIOPUR bit, and setting the GPIOPUR bit clears this one. A write takes effect on the second clock after it through the APB aperture, on the next clock through AHB. Writes to the JTAG/SWD and NMI pins' bits take effect only once GPIOLOCK is unlocked and the GPIOCR bit is set.

fields.name: SRL
fields.text: Turns on slew-rate limiting for each pin; it works only with 8-mA drive selected in GPIODR8R.

fields.name: DEN
fields.text: Turns on each pin's digital input and output, needed for GPIO or alternate-function use. With the bit clear the pin drives nothing and its input receiver is cut off. Resets to 0 on ports without special-consideration pins. Writes to the JTAG/SWD and NMI pins' bits take effect only once GPIOLOCK is unlocked and the GPIOCR bit is set.

fields.name: LOCK
fields.text: Writing 0x4C4F.434B unlocks GPIOCR for writing; any other value, or a write to GPIOCR, locks it again. A read gives the lock state.

fields.name: CR
fields.text: Per-pin commit enable for writes to GPIOAFSEL, GPIOPUR, GPIOPDR and GPIODEN; writable only while GPIOLOCK is unlocked. Only the NMI and four JTAG/SWD pins' bits are read-write and reset to 0; every other bit is fixed at 1.

values.text: Matching GPIOAFSEL, GPIOPUR, GPIOPDR, GPIODEN bits keep their value.
Matching GPIOAFSEL, GPIOPUR, GPIOPDR, GPIODEN bits take writes.

fields.name: GPIOAMSEL
fields.text: Turns off the analog isolation of each pin so it can serve as an ADC input. Valid only for pins with an analog function; resets to 0.

values.text: Analog off, isolation on; digital use per the other GPIO registers.

fields.name: PMC7
fields.text: Selects the peripheral function of pin 7.

fields.name: PMC6
fields.text: Selects the peripheral function of pin 6.

fields.name: PMC5
fields.text: Selects the peripheral function of pin 5.

fields.name: PMC4
fields.text: Selects the peripheral function of pin 4.

fields.name: PMC3
fields.text: Selects the peripheral function of pin 3.

fields.name: PMC2
fields.text: Selects the peripheral function of pin 2.

fields.name: PMC1
fields.text: Selects the peripheral function of pin 1.

fields.name: PMC0
fields.text: Selects the peripheral function of pin 0.

fields.name: ADCEN
fields.text: Makes each pin a trigger source for the ADC. With Port B's GPIOADCCTL clear, PB4 can still act as an external ADC trigger (legacy mode).

fields.name: DMAEN
fields.text: Makes each pin a trigger source for the μDMA.

fields.name: PID4
fields.text: Peripheral ID bits [7:0] of the 32-bit ID read across GPIOPeriphID4 to GPIOPeriphID7.

fields.name: PID5
fields.text: Peripheral ID bits [15:8] of the 32-bit ID read across GPIOPeriphID4 to GPIOPeriphID7.

fields.name: PID6
fields.text: Peripheral ID bits [23:16] of the 32-bit ID read across GPIOPeriphID4 to GPIOPeriphID7.

fields.name: PID7
fields.text: Peripheral ID bits [31:24] of the 32-bit ID read across GPIOPeriphID4 to GPIOPeriphID7.

fields.text: Peripheral ID bits [7:0]; software reads it to find this peripheral.

fields.name: PID1
fields.text: Peripheral ID bits [15:8]; software reads it to find this peripheral.

fields.name: PID2

fields.name: CID1
fields.text: PrimeCell ID bits [15:8], a common identifier across peripherals.

fields.name: CID2

fields.name: CID3
