fields.name: GPTMCFG
fields.text: Selects whether the timers run joined (32-bit, or 64-bit on a wide timer) or split into two halves (16-bit, or 32-bit on a wide timer); change only while GPTMCTL.TAEN and GPTMCTL.TBEN are both 0.

values.text: Joined timer: 32-bit on a 16/32-bit timer, 64-bit on a 32/64-bit wide timer.
Joined real-time clock counter: 32-bit on a 16/32-bit timer, 64-bit on a 32/64-bit wide timer.
Split timers: 16-bit each on a 16/32-bit timer, 32-bit each on a wide timer; each half's function is set by bits 1:0 of GPTMTAMR and GPTMTBMR.

fields.name: TAPLO
fields.text: Picks how the CCP pin behaves when GPTMTAILR reloads after Timer A reaches 0; used in PWM mode only.

values.text: Legacy: CCP pin is driven low when GPTMTAILR reloads after the count reaches 0.
CCP pin is driven high when GPTMTAILR reloads after the count reaches 0.

fields.name: TAMRSU
fields.text: Picks when a new GPTMTAMATCHR (and GPTMTAPR, if in use) takes effect; if set while TAEN is 0 they update when the timer is enabled, and while TASTALL is set they follow this bit.

values.text: GPTMTAMATCHR and GPTMTAPR (if used) update on the next cycle.
GPTMTAMATCHR and GPTMTAPR (if used) update on the next timeout.

fields.name: TAPWMIE
fields.text: In PWM mode only, enables an interrupt on the CCP output edges chosen by GPTMCTL.TAEVENT (rising, falling or both).

fields.name: TAILD
fields.text: Picks when a new GPTMTAILR value is loaded into GPTMTAR and GPTMTAV (and GPTMTAPR into GPTMTAPS and GPTMTAPV) while Timer A runs; no effect when counting up. If set while TAEN is 0 the registers load when the timer is enabled; while TASTALL is set, GPTMTAR and GPTMTAPS follow this bit.

values.text: Load GPTMTAR/GPTMTAV from GPTMTAILR and GPTMTAPS/GPTMTAPV from GPTMTAPR on the next cycle.
Load GPTMTAR/GPTMTAV from GPTMTAILR and GPTMTAPS/GPTMTAPV from GPTMTAPR on the next timeout.

fields.name: TASNAPS
fields.text: Turns on snap-shot mode for Timer A.

values.text: In periodic mode, Timer A's free-running, capture or snapshot value is copied into GPTMTAR at the time-out, capture or snapshot event; with the prescaler in use, the prescaler snapshot goes into GPTMTAPR.

fields.name: TAWOT
fields.text: Makes Timer A wait for a trigger from the timer before it in the daisy chain before counting; must be 0 for GP Timer Module 0, Timer A.

values.text: Timer A starts counting as soon as it is enabled.
Once enabled (GPTMCTL.TAEN set), Timer A starts counting only on a trigger from the previous timer in the daisy chain; applies to one-shot, periodic and PWM modes.

fields.name: TAMIE
fields.text: Enables the Timer A match interrupt in one-shot and periodic modes.

values.text: No match interrupt; with this bit 0 no µDMA or ADC match trigger is sent either, even if GPTMDMAEV.TATODMAEN or GPTMADCEV.TATOADCEN is set.
Interrupt raised when the count reaches the GPTMTAMATCHR value in one-shot or periodic mode.

fields.name: TACDIR
fields.text: Sets Timer A's count direction; ignored in PWM mode (always down) and RTC mode (always up).

fields.name: TAAMS
fields.text: Chooses between capture/compare and PWM for Timer A.

values.text: PWM mode; TACMR must also be 0 and TAMR set to 0x1 or 0x2.

fields.name: TACMR
fields.text: Chooses the capture mode for Timer A.

fields.name: TAMR
fields.text: Sets Timer A's mode, within the configuration chosen by GPTMCFG bits 2:0.

fields.name: TBPLO
fields.text: Picks how the CCP pin behaves when GPTMTBILR reloads after Timer B reaches 0; used in PWM mode only.

values.text: Legacy: CCP pin is driven low when GPTMTBILR reloads after the count reaches 0.
CCP pin is driven high when GPTMTBILR reloads after the count reaches 0.

fields.name: TBMRSU
fields.text: Picks when a new GPTMTBMATCHR (and GPTMTBPR, if in use) takes effect; if set while TBEN is 0 they update when the timer is enabled, and while TBSTALL is set they follow this bit.

values.text: GPTMTBMATCHR and GPTMTBPR (if used) update on the next cycle.
GPTMTBMATCHR and GPTMTBPR (if used) update on the next timeout.

fields.name: TBPWMIE
fields.text: In PWM mode only, enables an interrupt on the CCP output edges chosen by GPTMCTL.TBEVENT (rising, falling or both).

fields.name: TBILD
fields.text: Picks when a new GPTMTBILR value is loaded into GPTMTBR and GPTMTBV (and GPTMTBPR into GPTMTBPS and GPTMTBPV) while Timer B runs; no effect when counting up. If set while TBEN is 0 the registers load when the timer is enabled; while TBSTALL is set, GPTMTBR and GPTMTBPS follow this bit.

values.text: Load GPTMTBR/GPTMTBV from GPTMTBILR and GPTMTBPS/GPTMTBPV from GPTMTBPR on the next cycle.
Load GPTMTBR/GPTMTBV from GPTMTBILR and GPTMTBPS/GPTMTBPV from GPTMTBPR on the next timeout.

fields.name: TBSNAPS
fields.text: Turns on snap-shot mode for Timer B.

values.text: In periodic mode, Timer B's free-running value is copied into GPTMTBR at the time-out event; with the prescaler in use, the prescaler snapshot goes into GPTMTBPR.

fields.name: TBWOT
fields.text: Makes Timer B wait for a trigger from the timer before it in the daisy chain before counting.

values.text: Timer B starts counting as soon as it is enabled.
Once enabled (GPTMCTL.TBEN set), Timer B starts counting only on a trigger from the previous timer in the daisy chain; applies to one-shot, periodic and PWM modes.

fields.name: TBMIE
fields.text: Enables the Timer B match interrupt in one-shot and periodic modes.

values.text: No match interrupt; with this bit 0 no µDMA or ADC match trigger is sent either, even if GPTMDMAEV.TBTODMAEN or GPTMADCEV.TBTOADCEN is set.
Interrupt raised when the count reaches the GPTMTBMATCHR value in one-shot or periodic mode.

fields.name: TBCDIR
fields.text: Sets Timer B's count direction; ignored in PWM mode (always down) and RTC mode (always up).

fields.name: TBAMS
fields.text: Chooses between capture/compare and PWM for Timer B.

values.text: PWM mode; TBCMR must also be 0 and TBMR set to 0x1 or 0x2.

fields.name: TBCMR
fields.text: Chooses the capture mode for Timer B.

fields.name: TBMR
fields.text: Sets Timer B's mode, within the configuration chosen by GPTMCFG bits 2:0.

fields.name: TBPWML
fields.text: Sets the polarity of Timer B's PWM output.

fields.name: TBOTE
fields.text: Lets Timer B send a trigger to the ADC; the ADC must also be enabled and this timer chosen as a trigger source by the EMn bit in ADCEMUX.

values.text: Timer B ADC trigger on; a trigger comes only from a one-shot or periodic time-out, never from match or compare events.

fields.name: TBEVENT
fields.text: Chooses which CCP edges count as Timer B events; with PWM output inverted, the edge sense of the event interrupt flips (a positive-edge setting then fires on the negative edge).

fields.name: TBSTALL
fields.text: Decides whether Timer B stops while the debugger halts the processor; ignored during normal execution.

values.text: Timer B keeps counting while halted by the debugger.
Timer B stops counting while halted by the debugger.

fields.name: TBEN
fields.text: Turns Timer B on.

values.text: Timer B on: it starts counting, or its capture logic runs, as set by GPTMCFG.

fields.name: TAPWML
fields.text: Sets the polarity of Timer A's PWM output.

fields.name: TAOTE
fields.text: Lets Timer A send a trigger to the ADC; the ADC must also be enabled and this timer chosen as a trigger source by the EMn bit in ADCEMUX.

values.text: Timer A ADC trigger on; a trigger comes only from a one-shot or periodic time-out, never from match or compare events.

fields.name: RTCEN
fields.text: Decides whether RTC counting stops while the debugger halts the processor; when set, the timer never stalls in any mode, whatever TnSTALL says.

values.text: RTC counting stops while halted by the debugger.
RTC counting goes on while halted by the debugger.

fields.name: TAEVENT
fields.text: Chooses which CCP edges count as Timer A events; with PWM output inverted, the edge sense of the event interrupt flips (a positive-edge setting then fires on the negative edge).

fields.name: TASTALL
fields.text: Decides whether Timer A stops while the debugger halts the processor; ignored during normal execution.

values.text: Timer A keeps counting while halted by the debugger.
Timer A stops counting while halted by the debugger.

fields.name: TAEN
fields.text: Turns Timer A on.

values.text: Timer A on: it starts counting, or its capture logic runs, as set by GPTMCFG.

fields.name: WUEIM
fields.text: Unmasks the write update error interrupt of the 32/64-bit wide GPTM.

fields.name: TBMIM
fields.text: Unmasks the Timer B match interrupt.

fields.name: CBEIM
fields.text: Unmasks the Timer B capture mode event interrupt.

fields.name: CBMIM
fields.text: Unmasks the Timer B capture mode match interrupt.

fields.name: TBTOIM
fields.text: Unmasks the Timer B time-out interrupt.

fields.name: WUERIS
fields.text: Raw status of the write update error on the 32/64-bit wide GPTM.

values.text: Two writes in succession landed on the same Timer A or Timer B register, or Timer A's register got its write ahead of the matching Timer B one.

fields.name: TBMRIS
fields.text: Raw Timer B match flag; cleared by writing 1 to GPTMICR.TBMCINT.

values.text: With GPTMTBMR.TBMIE set, the count reached GPTMTBMATCHR (and GPTMTBPMR, if used) in one-shot or periodic mode.

fields.name: CBERIS
fields.text: Raw Timer B capture mode event flag; cleared by writing 1 to GPTMICR.CBECINT.

values.text: No Timer B capture mode event.
A Timer B capture mode event happened; raised in input edge-time mode, or in PWM mode when GPTMTBMR.TBPWMIE is set.

fields.name: CBMRIS
fields.text: Raw Timer B capture mode match flag; cleared by writing 1 to GPTMICR.CBMCINT.

values.text: No Timer B capture mode match.
In input edge-time mode, GPTMTBR and GPTMTBPR equalled GPTMTBMATCHR and GPTMTBPMR.

fields.name: TBTORIS
fields.text: Raw Timer B time-out flag; cleared by writing 1 to GPTMICR.TBTOCINT.

values.text: Timer B has not timed out.
Timer B timed out: in one-shot or periodic mode it reached its limit, 0 or the GPTMTBILR value depending on count direction.

fields.name: TAMRIS
fields.text: Raw Timer A match flag; cleared by writing 1 to GPTMICR.TAMCINT.

values.text: With GPTMTAMR.TAMIE set, the count reached GPTMTAMATCHR (and GPTMTAPMR, if used) in one-shot or periodic mode.

fields.name: RTCRIS

fields.name: CAERIS

fields.name: CAMRIS

values.text: No Timer A capture mode match.
In input edge-time mode, GPTMTAR and GPTMTAPR equalled GPTMTAMATCHR and GPTMTAPMR.

fields.name: TATORIS

values.text: Timer A has not timed out.
Timer A timed out: in one-shot or periodic mode it reached its limit, 0 or the GPTMTAILR value depending on count direction.

fields.text: Write 1 to clear GPTMRIS.WUERIS and GPTMMIS.WUEMIS.

fields.name: TAILR
fields.text: A write loads Timer A's counter; a read gives back the GPTMTAILR value.

registers.name: GPTMTBILR
registers.title: GPTM Timer B Interval Load
notes: The field table gives TBILR's reset as 0x0000.FFFF.

fields.name: TBILR
fields.text: A write loads Timer B's counter; a read gives back the GPTMTBILR value. With a 16/32-bit GPTM in 32-bit mode, writes have no effect and reads still give the GPTMTBILR value.

fields.name: TAMR
fields.text: Value checked against GPTMTAR to detect match events.

registers.name: GPTMTBMATCHR
registers.title: GPTM Timer B Match
notes: The field table gives TBMR's reset as 0x0000.FFFF.

fields.name: TBMR
fields.text: Value checked against GPTMTBR to detect match events.

fields.name: TAPSRH
fields.text: Upper 8 bits of Timer A's 16-bit prescaler on the 32/64-bit wide GPTM; reserved on the 16/32-bit GPTM. Written to load, read to get the current value.

fields.name: TAPSR
fields.text: Timer A's prescaler: all 8 bits on the 16/32-bit GPTM, the lower 8 bits of the 16-bit prescaler on the 32/64-bit wide GPTM. Written to load, read to get the current value.

fields.name: TBPSRH
fields.text: Upper 8 bits of Timer B's 16-bit prescaler on the 32/64-bit wide GPTM; reserved on the 16/32-bit GPTM. Written to load, read to get the current value.

fields.name: TBPSR
fields.text: Timer B's prescaler: all 8 bits on the 16/32-bit GPTM, the lower 8 bits of the 16-bit prescaler on the 32/64-bit wide GPTM. Written to load, read to get the current value.

fields.name: TAPSMRH
fields.text: Upper 8 bits of Timer A's 16-bit prescale match value on the 32/64-bit wide GPTM, used with GPTMTAMATCHR to find match events when the prescaler is in use; reserved on the 16/32-bit GPTM.

fields.name: TAPSMR
fields.text: Timer A's prescale match value, used with GPTMTAMATCHR to find match events when the prescaler is in use: all 8 bits on the 16/32-bit GPTM, the lower 8 of 16 bits on the 32/64-bit wide GPTM.

fields.name: TBPSMRH
fields.text: Upper 8 bits of Timer B's 16-bit prescale match value on the 32/64-bit wide GPTM, used with GPTMTBMATCHR to find match events when the prescaler is in use; reserved on the 16/32-bit GPTM.

fields.name: TBPSMR
fields.text: Timer B's prescale match value, used with GPTMTBMATCHR to find match events when the prescaler is in use: all 8 bits on the 16/32-bit GPTM, the lower 8 of 16 bits on the 32/64-bit wide GPTM.

fields.name: TAR
fields.text: Reads Timer A's current count, except in input edge modes: in edge-count mode it holds the number of edges seen, in edge-time mode the time of the latest edge event.

registers.name: GPTMTBR
registers.title: GPTM Timer B
notes: The field table gives TBR's reset as 0x0000.FFFF.

fields.name: TBR
fields.text: Reads Timer B's current count, except in input edge modes: in edge-count mode it holds the number of edges seen, in edge-time mode the time of the latest edge event.

fields.name: TAV
fields.text: Reads Timer A's current free-running value in every mode; a written value is loaded into GPTMTAR on the next clock cycle. In 16-bit mode only the lower 16 bits accept a write; writes to the prescaler bits do nothing.

registers.name: GPTMTBV
registers.title: GPTM Timer B Value
notes: The field table gives TBV's reset as 0x0000.FFFF.

fields.name: TBV
fields.text: Reads Timer B's current free-running value in every mode; a written value is loaded into GPTMTBR on the next clock cycle. In 16-bit mode only the lower 16 bits accept a write; writes to the prescaler bits do nothing.

fields.name: RTCPD
fields.text: Current RTC predivider count while the timer runs in RTC mode; meaningless in other modes.

fields.name: PSS
fields.text: Reads the current Timer A prescaler value.

fields.name: PSS
fields.text: Reads the current Timer B prescaler value.

fields.name: PSV
fields.text: Reads Timer A's prescaler current free-running value.

fields.name: PSV
fields.text: Reads Timer B's prescaler current free-running value.

fields.name: SIZE
fields.text: Gives the width of this module's counters.

values.text: Timer A and Timer B are 16-bit counters, each with an 8-bit prescaler.
Timer A and Timer B are 32-bit counters, each with a 16-bit prescaler.

fields.name: WDTLOAD
fields.text: Interval the 32-bit counter counts down from; a write loads it at once and restarts the count, and a value of 0 raises an interrupt immediately.

fields.name: WDTVALUE
fields.text: Present count of the 32-bit down counter.

registers.name: WDTCTL
registers.title: Watchdog Control
notes: A time-out can raise an interrupt, or a reset when the count expires a second time.

WDT1 runs from its own clock, so back-to-back writes, or a write then a read, to WDT1 registers need a gap; poll WRC for 1 before the next access. Back-to-back reads are unrestricted. WDT0 runs from the system clock and has no such limit.

fields.name: WRC
fields.text: Write complete flag for WDT1: cleared by a write and set when that write has finished. On WDT0 the bit is reserved, with a reset value of 0.

values.text: A WDT1 register write is still under way.
No write under way; WDT1 registers may be accessed.

fields.name: INTTYPE
fields.text: Chooses whether the watchdog interrupt is ordinary or non-maskable.

fields.name: RESEN
fields.text: Turns on the watchdog's reset output.

fields.name: INTEN
fields.text: Turns on the watchdog interrupt and starts the timer; once set, writes to it are ignored until a hardware reset or a software reset through SRWD.

values.text: Interrupt off; after being set it clears only by hardware reset or an SRWD software reset.
Interrupt on and timer running; further writes have no effect.

registers.name: WDTICR
registers.title: Watchdog Interrupt Clear
notes: WDTLOCK does not lock WDTICR, so the interrupt can always be cleared; a write at any time clears WDTMIS and reloads the counter.

fields.name: WDTINTCLR
fields.text: Writing any value clears the watchdog interrupt and reloads the counter from WDTLOAD; this is how a time-out interrupt is serviced. Reads and reset value are undefined.

fields.name: WDTRIS
fields.text: Raw time-out interrupt flag, readable even when the interrupt is masked.

fields.name: WDTMIS
fields.text: Time-out interrupt flag after masking: the raw flag ANDed with the interrupt enable.

values.text: Time-out passed to the interrupt controller.

fields.name: STALL
fields.text: Watchdog stall enable: whether the counter halts while a debugger has stopped the CPU.

values.text: Counter keeps running while the CPU is halted by a debugger.
Counter pauses while the CPU is halted by a debugger and carries on when it restarts.

registers.name: WDTLOCK
registers.title: Watchdog Lock
notes: The lock takes effect 2 clock cycles after the write.

fields.name: WDTLOCK
fields.text: Writing 0x1ACC.E551 opens the watchdog registers to writes; writing anything else locks them again, all but WDTTEST, which is not to be written while locked. A read gives the lock state, not the value written.

values.text: A digital comparator interrupt is pending in ADCDCISC.

fields.name: CIE
fields.text: Turns on the comparison interrupt of this digital comparator.

values.text: Comparison interrupt off; conversion data cannot raise it.
Comparison interrupt on; conversion data raises it as CIC and CIM set.

fields.name: CIC
fields.text: Region, set by COMP0 and COMP1 in ADCDCCMPn, in which conversion data raises the interrupt.

values.text: Low band: ADC data < COMP0 <= COMP1.
Mid band: COMP0 <= ADC data < COMP1.
High band: COMP0 < COMP1 <= ADC data.

fields.name: CIM
fields.text: How the comparison raises the interrupt.

values.text: Always: interrupt on every conversion whose data lies in the chosen region.
Once: interrupt only when the data first enters the chosen region.
Hysteresis always: interrupt on every conversion in the chosen region until the data enters the opposite region, which clears the hysteresis.
Hysteresis once: one interrupt when the data first lies in the chosen region, then none until the data enters the opposite region and clears the hysteresis.

fields.name: OE
fields.text: UART overrun error.

values.text: No data lost to FIFO overrun.
A character arrived with the FIFO full and data was lost.

fields.name: BE
fields.text: Break error; in FIFO mode it belongs to the character at the FIFO top. A break puts a single 0 character in the FIFO, and reception resumes only after the input returns to 1 (marking) and a valid start bit arrives.

values.text: Break seen: receive input held Low longer than one full frame (start, data, parity and stop bits).

fields.name: PE
fields.text: Parity error; in FIFO mode it belongs to the character at the FIFO top.

values.text: Received parity disagrees with the parity set by UARTLCRH bits 2 and 7.

fields.name: FE
fields.text: UART framing error.

values.text: The character lacked a valid stop bit (stop bit must be 1).

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Write a byte here to send it; read to get the received byte.

fields.name: OE
fields.text: Overrun error; a write to UARTECR clears it. When the FIFO is full no more data enters it, so the FIFO stays valid and only the shift register is overwritten; the CPU has to read data out to empty the FIFO.

values.text: No data lost to FIFO overrun.
Data arrived while the FIFO was full and was lost.

fields.name: BE
fields.text: Break error; a write to UARTECR clears it. In FIFO mode it goes with the character at the FIFO top. A break loads a single 0 character into the FIFO, and the next character is taken only once the receive input returns to 1 (marking) and a valid start bit arrives.

values.text: Break seen: receive input held Low longer than one full frame (start, data, parity and stop bits).

fields.name: PE
fields.text: Parity error; a write to UARTECR clears it.

values.text: Received parity disagrees with the parity set by UARTLCRH bits 2 and 7.

fields.name: FE
fields.text: Framing error; a write to UARTECR clears it. In FIFO mode it goes with the character at the FIFO top.

values.text: The received character lacked a valid stop bit (stop bit must be 1).

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Any value written here resets the overrun, break, parity and framing error flags.

fields.name: TXFE
fields.text: Transmit FIFO empty; its meaning follows UARTLCRH.FEN.

values.text: Transmit holding register empty (FEN = 0), or transmit FIFO empty (FEN = 1).

fields.name: RXFF
fields.text: Receive FIFO full; its meaning follows UARTLCRH.FEN.

values.text: Receive holding register full (FEN = 0), or receive FIFO full (FEN = 1).

fields.name: TXFF
fields.text: Transmit FIFO full; its meaning follows UARTLCRH.FEN.

values.text: Transmit holding register full (FEN = 0), or transmit FIFO full (FEN = 1).

fields.name: RXFE
fields.text: Receive FIFO empty; its meaning follows UARTLCRH.FEN.

values.text: Receive holding register empty (FEN = 0), or receive FIFO empty (FEN = 1).

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Busy; goes set the moment the transmit FIFO holds data, whether or not the UART is enabled.

values.text: Transmitting; stays set until the whole byte and its stop bits leave the shift register.

fields.name: CTS
fields.text: Clear To Send.

fields.name: ILPDVSR
fields.text: 8-bit divisor applied to SysClk to make the IrDA low-power IrLPBaud16 clock.

fields.name: DIVINT
fields.text: Integer Baud-Rate Divisor: whole-number part of the baud divisor.

fields.name: DIVFRAC
fields.text: Fractional Baud-Rate Divisor: fractional part of the baud divisor.

fields.name: SPS
fields.text: Stick parity: with PEN, EPS and SPS set, parity is sent and checked as 0; with PEN and SPS set and EPS clear, as 1. Clear turns stick parity off.

fields.name: WLEN
fields.text: Data bits per frame, sent or received.

fields.name: FEN
fields.text: Turns the transmit and receive FIFOs on.

values.text: FIFOs off (character mode); each acts as a 1-byte holding register.

fields.name: STP2
fields.text: Selects two stop bits.

values.text: One stop bit sent per frame.
Two stop bits sent per frame; reception does not check for two. Forced to 2 in 7816 smart card mode (UARTCTL.SMART set).

fields.name: EPS
fields.text: Even parity select; no effect while PEN disables parity.

values.text: Even parity on transmit and receive: even count of 1s across data and parity bits.

fields.name: PEN
fields.text: Parity enable.

values.text: No parity bit in the frame.

fields.name: BRK
fields.text: Sends a break.

values.text: UnTx is driven Low continuously once the current character finishes; hold set for at least two frame times for a proper break.

fields.name: CTSEN
fields.text: Clear To Send flow control enable.

values.text: CTS flow control on; data goes out only while U1CTS is asserted.

fields.name: RTSEN
fields.text: Request to Send flow control enable.

values.text: RTS flow control on; U1RTS asserts to request data only while the receive FIFO has space.

fields.name: RTS
fields.text: With RTSEN clear, this bit drives U1RTS. With RTSEN set, writes are ignored and reads carry no meaning.

fields.name: RXE
fields.text: Receive enable; UARTEN must also be set to receive. Disabled mid-character, the receiver finishes that character first.

fields.name: TXE
fields.text: Transmit enable; UARTEN must also be set to transmit. Disabled mid-character, the transmitter finishes that character first.

fields.name: LBE
fields.text: Loop back enable.

values.text: UnTx is routed back into UnRx.

fields.name: HSE
fields.text: High-speed enable; the clock used also depends on the baud divisor. Has no effect on clocking in ISO 7816 smart card mode (SMART set).

fields.name: EOT
fields.text: Selects when UARTRIS.TXRIS goes set.

values.text: TXRIS sets when the transmit FIFO meets the UARTIFLS condition.
TXRIS sets only once all data, stop bits included, has left the serializer.

fields.name: SMART
fields.text: ISO 7816 smart card mode. Software must set UARTLCRH to 8-bit words (WLEN = 0x3) and even parity (PEN = 1, EPS = 1, SPS = 0). STP2 is ignored and two stop bits are used. No automatic retransmit on parity error: a transmit parity error stops all further transmission and software must resend.

fields.name: SIRLP
fields.text: IrDA SIR low-power encoding select; lowers power but may shorten range.

values.text: Low bits sent as a High pulse 3/16 of a bit period wide.
SIR low-power mode: Low bits sent as pulses 3 IrLPBaud16 periods wide, at any bit rate.

fields.name: SIREN
fields.text: IrDA SIR enable.

values.text: IrDA SIR block on; the UART sends and receives with the SIR protocol.

fields.name: UARTEN
fields.text: UART enable. Disabled mid-character, the UART finishes that character first.

fields.name: RXIFLSEL
fields.text: Receive FIFO fill level that triggers the receive interrupt.

fields.name: TXIFLSEL
fields.text: Transmit FIFO level that triggers the transmit interrupt. Ignored when UARTCTL.EOT is set; the interrupt then comes once the FIFO is empty and all data and stop bits have left the serializer.

fields.name: 9BITIM
fields.text: Interrupt mask for UARTRIS.9BITRIS.

values.text: UARTRIS.9BITRIS is held back from the interrupt controller.
UARTRIS.9BITRIS going set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: OEIM
fields.text: Interrupt mask for UARTRIS.OERIS.

values.text: UARTRIS.OERIS is held back from the interrupt controller.
UARTRIS.OERIS going set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: BEIM
fields.text: Interrupt mask for UARTRIS.BERIS.

values.text: UARTRIS.BERIS is held back from the interrupt controller.
UARTRIS.BERIS going set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: PEIM
fields.text: Interrupt mask for UARTRIS.PERIS.

values.text: UARTRIS.PERIS is held back from the interrupt controller.
UARTRIS.PERIS going set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: FEIM

UARTRIS.FERIS going set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: RTIM

UARTRIS.RTRIS going set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: TXIM
fields.text: Interrupt mask for UARTRIS.TXRIS.

values.text: UARTRIS.TXRIS is held back from the interrupt controller.
UARTRIS.TXRIS going set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: RXIM
fields.text: Interrupt mask for UARTRIS.RXRIS.

values.text: UARTRIS.RXRIS is held back from the interrupt controller.
UARTRIS.RXRIS going set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: CTSIM
fields.text: Interrupt mask for UARTRIS.CTSRIS. Present on UART1 only; reserved on UART0 and UART2.

values.text: UARTRIS.CTSRIS is held back from the interrupt controller.
UARTRIS.CTSRIS going set raises an interrupt at the interrupt controller.

fields.name: 9BITRIS
fields.text: Raw status; writing 1 to UARTICR.9BITIC clears it.

fields.name: OERIS

fields.name: RTRIS
fields.text: Raw status; writing 1 to UARTICR.RTIC clears it. UARTIM.RTIM must be set for RTRIS to show the receive timeout.

fields.name: TXRIS
fields.text: Raw status; writing 1 to UARTICR.TXIC clears it. It also clears once the transmit FIFO is filled above its trigger level (FIFO on) or one byte is written (FIFO off).

values.text: With UARTCTL.EOT clear, the transmit FIFO passed the UARTIFLS level; with EOT set, the last bit of all data has left the serializer.

fields.name: RXRIS
fields.text: Raw status; writing 1 to UARTICR.RXIC clears it. It also clears once the receive FIFO is read below its trigger level (FIFO on) or one byte is read (FIFO off).

values.text: Receive FIFO passed the UARTIFLS level.

fields.name: CTSRIS
fields.text: Raw status; writing 1 to UARTICR.CTSIC clears it. Present on UART1 only; reserved on UART0 and UART2.

values.text: Clear To Send event, as used in software flow control.

fields.name: 9BITMIS
fields.text: Masked status; writing 1 to UARTICR.9BITIC clears it.

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from a received address match.

fields.name: OEMIS
fields.text: Masked status; writing 1 to UARTICR.OEIC clears it.

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from an overrun error.

fields.name: BEMIS
fields.text: Masked status; writing 1 to UARTICR.BEIC clears it.

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from a break error.

fields.name: PEMIS
fields.text: Masked status; writing 1 to UARTICR.PEIC clears it.

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from a parity error.

fields.name: FEMIS
fields.text: Masked status; writing 1 to UARTICR.FEIC clears it.

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from a framing error.

fields.name: RTMIS
fields.text: Masked status; writing 1 to UARTICR.RTIC clears it. UARTIM.RTIM must be set for RTMIS to show the receive timeout.

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from a receive timeout.

fields.name: TXMIS
fields.text: Masked status; writing 1 to UARTICR.TXIC clears it. It also clears once the transmit FIFO is filled above its trigger level (FIFO on) or one byte is written (FIFO off).

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from the transmit FIFO passing its level (EOT clear) or the last data bit going out (EOT set).

fields.name: RXMIS
fields.text: Masked status; writing 1 to UARTICR.RXIC clears it. It also clears once the receive FIFO is read below its trigger level (FIFO on) or one byte is read (FIFO off).

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from the receive FIFO passing its level.

fields.name: CTSMIS
fields.text: Masked status; writing 1 to UARTICR.CTSIC clears it. Present on UART1 only; reserved on UART0 and UART2.

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from Clear To Send.

fields.name: 9BITIC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear UARTRIS.9BITRIS and UARTMIS.9BITMIS.

fields.name: OEIC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear UARTRIS.OERIS and UARTMIS.OEMIS.

fields.name: BEIC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear UARTRIS.BERIS and UARTMIS.BEMIS.

fields.text: Write 1 to clear UARTRIS.PERIS and UARTMIS.PEMIS.

fields.name: FEIC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear UARTRIS.FERIS and UARTMIS.FEMIS.

fields.name: RTIC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear UARTRIS.RTRIS and UARTMIS.RTMIS.

fields.text: Write 1 to clear UARTRIS.TXRIS and UARTMIS.TXMIS.

fields.text: Write 1 to clear UARTRIS.RXRIS and UARTMIS.RXMIS.

fields.name: DMAERR
fields.text: Stops µDMA receive requests on a receive error.

values.text: Receive errors leave µDMA receive requests alone.
A receive error turns µDMA receive requests off.

fields.name: RXDMAE
fields.text: µDMA enable for the receive FIFO.

fields.text: Turns on 9-bit mode.

fields.name: MASK

fields.text: Reports 9-bit data support for RS-485.

fields.text: Selects the clock source for the UART baud clock.

values.text: System clock (from clock source and divider).

fields.name: SCR
fields.text: Sets the SSI bit rate for transmit and receive with CPSDVSR: BR = SysClk / (CPSDVSR x (1 + SCR)), SCR 0 to 255, CPSDVSR an even value 2 to 254 in SSICPSR.

fields.name: SPH
fields.text: Freescale SPI format only: picks which clock edge samples data and lets it change; this decides whether a clock transition comes before the first sampling edge.

values.text: Sample on the first clock edge.
Sample on the second clock edge.

fields.name: SPO
fields.text: Idle level of SSInClk.

values.text: SSInClk idles high between transfers; the SSInClk pin must then also be set as pull-up in GPIOPUR.

fields.name: FRF
fields.text: Picks the frame format.

fields.name: DSS
fields.text: Number of bits in a data frame.

fields.name: EOT
fields.text: Picks when TXRIS fires; valid only in master mode (MS = 0). In Freescale SPI mode, with EOT at 0 in an on-chip slave SSI that the uDMA feeds to an on-chip master SSI over external loopback, the slave raises an EOT interrupt on every byte even while the FIFO is full.

values.text: TXRIS fires once the TX FIFO holds half its depth or fewer entries.

fields.name: MS
fields.text: Chooses master or slave; change it only while SSE is 0.

fields.name: SSE
fields.text: Turns the SSI on or off.

values.text: Enabled; clear it before changing any control register.

fields.name: LBM
fields.text: Loops the transmit shifter back to the receive shifter inside the chip.

values.text: Transmit shifter output feeds the receive shifter input internally.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Reading takes the next entry from the receive FIFO; writing puts an entry into the transmit FIFO. Frames under 16 bits are written right-justified, with the upper unused bits ignored on transmit; received frames come back right-justified.

fields.name: BSY
fields.text: Shows whether the SSI is busy.

values.text: A frame is being sent or received, or the transmit FIFO has data.

fields.name: RFF
fields.text: Set while the receive FIFO is full.

fields.name: RNE
fields.text: Set while the receive FIFO holds data.

fields.name: TNF
fields.text: Set while the transmit FIFO has room.

fields.name: TFE
fields.text: Set while the transmit FIFO is empty.

fields.name: CPSDVSR
fields.text: Prescale divisor from the system clock to SSInClk, an even number 2 to 254 chosen for the SSInClk frequency; bit 0 always reads 0.

fields.name: TXIM
fields.text: Lets the transmit FIFO interrupt reach the interrupt controller.

fields.name: RXIM
fields.text: Lets the receive FIFO interrupt reach the interrupt controller.

fields.name: RTIM
fields.text: Lets the receive time-out interrupt reach the interrupt controller.

fields.name: RORIM

fields.name: TXRIS
fields.text: Unmasked transmit FIFO interrupt; goes to 0 once the transmit FIFO is over half full (EOT = 0) or holds any data (EOT = 1).

values.text: With EOT = 0, the TX FIFO is at half empty or less; with EOT = 1, the TX FIFO has emptied and its final bit has been shifted out.

fields.name: RXRIS
fields.text: Unmasked receive FIFO interrupt; goes to 0 once the receive FIFO drops under half full.

values.text: Receive FIFO is half full or more.

fields.name: RTRIS
fields.text: Unmasked receive time-out interrupt; writing 1 to SSIICR.RTIC clears it.

fields.name: RORRIS
fields.text: Unmasked receive overrun interrupt; writing 1 to SSIICR.RORIC clears it.

fields.name: TXMIS
fields.text: Masked transmit FIFO interrupt; goes to 0 once the transmit FIFO is over half empty (EOT = 0) or holds any data (EOT = 1).

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from the transmit FIFO at half empty or less (EOT = 0) or from the last data bit sent (EOT = 1).

fields.name: RXMIS
fields.text: Masked receive FIFO interrupt; goes to 0 once the receive FIFO drops under half full.

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from the receive FIFO at half full or more.

fields.name: RTMIS
fields.text: Masked receive time-out interrupt; writing 1 to SSIICR.RTIC clears it.

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from a receive time-out.

fields.name: RORMIS
fields.text: Masked receive overrun interrupt; writing 1 to SSIICR.RORIC clears it.

values.text: No interrupt, or it is masked.
Unmasked interrupt from a receive FIFO overflow.

fields.text: Seven-bit address of the slave, A6 to A0.

fields.name: R/S
fields.text: Direction of the next master operation: receive when 1, transmit when 0.

fields.name: CLKTO
fields.text: Flags a clock timeout error; a STOP sent by the master or a master reset clears it.

fields.name: BUSBSY
fields.text: Shows whether the I2C bus is in use, following START and STOP conditions.

fields.name: IDLE
fields.text: Shows whether the I2C controller is idle.

fields.name: ARBLST
fields.text: Shows whether the controller lost bus arbitration.

fields.name: DATACK
fields.text: Shows whether the data sent was acknowledged.

fields.name: ADRACK
fields.text: Shows whether the address sent was acknowledged.

fields.name: ERROR

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Shows the controller is busy; the rest of the status bits mean nothing until it clears.

registers.name: I2CMCS
registers.title: I2C Master Control/Status
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00000020.

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Selects High-Speed mode for the master.

values.text: Standard, Fast or Fast mode plus, picked by the I2CMTPR value giving 100 kbps, 400 kbps or 1 Mbps on SCL.

fields.name: ACK
fields.text: Has the master acknowledge each received data byte by itself.

fields.name: STOP
fields.text: Has the controller send a STOP condition.

fields.name: START
fields.text: Has the controller send a START or repeated START condition.

fields.name: RUN
fields.text: Lets the master transmit or receive.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: The byte sent or received in a master transfer.

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Selects whether the SCL period set by TPR is for High-speed mode or for the slower modes.

values.text: TPR period is for Standard (100 Kbps), Fast (400 Kbps) or Fast-mode plus (1 Mbps).
TPR period is for High-speed mode (3.33 Mbps).

fields.name: TPR
fields.text: Sets the SCL period, 1 to 127: SCL_PERIOD = 2 x (1 + TPR) x (SCL_LP + SCL_HP) x CLK_PRD, with SCL_LP fixed at 6, SCL_HP fixed at 4 and CLK_PRD the system clock period in ns.

fields.name: CLKIM
fields.text: Lets the clock timeout interrupt reach the interrupt controller.

values.text: CLKRIS kept from the interrupt controller.
Interrupt sent when I2CMRIS.CLKRIS is set.

fields.name: IM
fields.text: Lets the master interrupt reach the interrupt controller.

values.text: RIS kept from the interrupt controller.
Interrupt sent when I2CMRIS.RIS is set.

fields.name: CLKRIS

fields.text: Raw master interrupt flag; a 1 written to I2CMICR.IC clears it.

fields.name: CLKMIS
fields.text: Masked clock timeout interrupt flag; a 1 written to I2CMICR.CLKIC clears it.

values.text: Unmasked clock timeout interrupt signaled, pending.

fields.name: MIS
fields.text: Masked master interrupt flag; a 1 written to I2CMICR.IC clears it.

fields.name: CLKIC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear I2CMRIS.CLKRIS and I2CMMIS.CLKMIS; reads give nothing useful.

fields.name: IC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear I2CMRIS.RIS and I2CMMIS.MIS; reads give nothing useful.

fields.name: GFE
fields.text: Turns on the I2C glitch filter, whose pulse width is set by I2CMCR2.GFPW.

fields.name: SFE
fields.text: Turns on the slave function.

fields.name: MFE
fields.text: Turns on the master function.

fields.name: LPBK
fields.text: Puts the controller in test-mode loopback.

registers.name: I2CMCLKOCNT
registers.title: I2C Master Clock Low Timeout Count

fields.name: CNTL
fields.text: Top 8 bits of the 12-bit clock-low timeout counter, whose low 4 bits are always 0; must be above 0x1. The counter runs down while SCL stays low and reloads from this value whenever SCL is released.

fields.name: SDA
fields.text: Present level of I2CSDA.

fields.name: SCL
fields.text: Present level of I2CSCL.

fields.name: GFPW
fields.text: Width, in system clocks, of the pulses the glitch filter removes from SCL and SDA.

fields.name: OAR
fields.text: The device's own seven-bit slave address, A6 to A0.

fields.name: OAR2SEL
fields.text: Shows the OAR2 address was the one matched; updated at each address comparison.

values.text: No match, or matched in legacy mode.
OAR2 address matched and ACKed by the slave.

fields.name: FBR
fields.text: Set once the first byte after the slave's own address is received; valid only while RREQ is set, cleared by reading I2CSDR, unused in slave transmit.

values.text: First byte after own address received.

fields.name: TREQ
fields.text: Shows the controller, addressed as slave transmitter, is stretching the clock until I2CSDR is written.

values.text: Addressed as slave transmitter; master held by clock stretching until I2CSDR is written.

fields.name: RREQ
fields.text: Shows received data waiting from the master, with the clock stretched until I2CSDR is read.

values.text: Data from the master waiting; master held by clock stretching until I2CSDR is read.

fields.name: DA
fields.text: Turns on slave operation; once set, do not set it again until a write of 0 or a reset clears it, or transfers may fail.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: The byte sent or received in a slave transfer.

fields.name: STOPIM

fields.text: Write 1 to clear I2CSRIS.STOPRIS and I2CSMIS.STOPMIS; reads give nothing useful.

fields.text: Write 1 to clear I2CSRIS.STARTRIS and I2CSMIS.STARTMIS; reads give nothing useful.

fields.text: Write 1 to clear I2CSRIS.STOPRIS and I2CSMIS.STOPMIS; reads give nothing useful.

fields.text: Response sent when the override is on: ACK for valid data or command, NACK for invalid.

fields.text: Reads 1 when the module can run in High-speed mode.

values.text: Standard, Fast or Fast mode plus.

registers.name: CANCTL
registers.title: CAN Control
notes: Setting or clearing INIT does not shorten bus-off recovery. On going bus-off the controller sets INIT and all bus activity stops; once the CPU clears INIT it waits for 129 runs of 11 High bits (bus idle) before normal operation resumes, and the error counters are reset at the end. Each run of 11 High bits seen in that wait writes code 0x5 to CANSTS.LEC, so software can tell a bus stuck Low or disturbed and follow the recovery.

fields.name: TEST
fields.text: Puts the CAN controller into test mode.

fields.name: CCE
fields.text: Lets software write the CANBIT register.

values.text: CANBIT can be written while INIT is 1.

fields.name: DAR
fields.text: Turns off automatic resending of disturbed messages.

fields.name: EIE
fields.text: Enables the error interrupt, raised by a change of CANSTS.BOFF or CANSTS.EWARN.

values.text: A change of BOFF or EWARN in CANSTS raises an interrupt.

fields.name: SIE
fields.text: Enables the status interrupt, raised by a change of CANSTS.TXOK, RXOK or LEC.

values.text: An interrupt follows each successful transmit or receive and each detected bus error, that is any change of TXOK, RXOK or LEC in CANSTS.

fields.name: IE
fields.text: Master enable for CAN interrupts.

fields.name: INIT
fields.text: Holds the controller in initialization; the controller sets it itself on going bus-off.

registers.name: CANSTS
registers.title: CAN Status
notes: Reading CANSTS has side effects: it clears a pending CANINT. LEC is cleared when a message is sent or received without error; software may write the unused code 0x7 to LEC and watch for it to change. BOFF and EWARN raise the error interrupt, and RXOK, TXOK and LEC the status interrupt, when enabled in CANCTL; a change of EPASS or a write to RXOK, TXOK or LEC raises none.

fields.name: BOFF
fields.text: Shows whether the controller is bus-off.

fields.name: EWARN
fields.text: Shows that an error counter has reached the warning limit of 96.

values.text: One or both error counters at 96 or more.

fields.name: EPASS
fields.text: Shows whether the module is error passive.

values.text: Error active: receive or transmit error count at 127 or under.
Error passive: receive or transmit error count over 127.

fields.name: RXOK
fields.text: Set when a message has been received without error; software clears it by writing 0.

values.text: No message received without error since the last clear.
A message has been received without error since the last clear, whatever the acceptance filter decided.

fields.name: TXOK
fields.text: Set when a message has been sent without error; software clears it by writing 0.

values.text: No message sent without error since the last clear.
A message has been sent without error and acknowledged by one or more other nodes since the last clear.

fields.name: LEC
fields.text: Code for the kind of error last seen on the CAN bus.

values.text: Stuff error: over 5 bits of the same level in a row where a received message forbids it.
Format error: a fixed-format part of a received frame is malformed.
ACK error: no other node acknowledged the sent message.
Bit 1 error: sending a High (1), the controller read the bus as Low (0). Such a conflict counts as an error in every field but the arbitration field, where it is part of arbitration.

Bit 0 error: the controller meant to send a Low (0) but read the bus as High (1); during bus-off recovery this code is set after every run of 11 High bits, so software can follow the recovery without disturbing the bus.
CRC error: the CRC of a received message did not match the one computed.
No event: no bus event since software wrote this code into LEC.

fields.name: RP
fields.text: Shows whether the receive error counter is at the error passive level.

values.text: Receive error counter at 127 or less.
Receive error counter at 128 or more.

fields.name: REC
fields.text: Present count of the receive error counter, 0 to 127.

fields.name: TEC
fields.text: Present count of the transmit error counter, 0 to 255.

registers.name: CANBIT
registers.title: CAN Bit Timing
notes: Writable only while CANCTL.CCE and CANCTL.INIT are set. Values are set against the system clock.

fields.name: TSEG2
fields.text: Phase 2 length after the sample point, in bit time quanta; the hardware uses the value plus 1, so the reset value 0x2 gives 3 quanta. Range 0x0 to 0x7; quantum set by BRP.

fields.name: TSEG1
fields.text: Phase 1 length before the sample point, in bit time quanta; the hardware uses the value plus 1, so the reset value 0x3 gives 4 quanta. Range 0x0 to 0xF; quantum set by BRP.

fields.name: SJW
fields.text: Amount, in bit time quanta, by which the controller can lengthen or shorten TSEG1 or TSEG2 when it sees a phase error at start of frame; the hardware uses the value plus 1, so reset 0 gives 1 quantum. Range 0x0 to 0x3.

fields.name: BRP
fields.text: Divider from the CAN clock to the bit time quantum: the count of CAN clock periods in one quantum is the value plus 1 (reset gives 2). Range 0x00 to 0x3F; a bit time is a whole number of quanta; CANBRPE extends the divider.

registers.name: CANINT

fields.name: INTID

values.text: The message object with this number raised the interrupt.

fields.name: LBACK

fields.name: SILENT

fields.name: BASIC

fields.name: BRPE

fields.name: NEWDAT
fields.text: NEWDAT bit of each of the 16 message objects.

values.text: The message handler has written no new data into that object since the CPU last cleared the flag.
That object holds new data, written by the CPU or the message handler.

registers.name: CANMSG1INT
registers.title: CAN Message 1 Interrupt Pending
notes: CANMSG1INT holds the INTPND bits of message objects 1 to 16 and CANMSG2INT those of objects 17 to 32. An INTPND bit is changed by the CPU through CANIFnMCTL or by the message handler after a frame is received or sent; CANINT also encodes it.

fields.name: INTPND
fields.text: INTPND bit of each of the 16 message objects.

values.text: That message object is not an interrupt source.
That message object is an interrupt source.

registers.name: CANMSG2INT
registers.title: CAN Message 2 Interrupt Pending
notes: CANMSG1INT holds the INTPND bits of message objects 1 to 16 and CANMSG2INT those of objects 17 to 32. An INTPND bit is changed by the CPU through CANIFnMCTL or by the message handler after a frame is received or sent; CANINT also encodes it.

fields.name: INTPND
fields.text: INTPND bit of each of the 16 message objects.

values.text: That message object is not an interrupt source.
That message object is an interrupt source.

registers.name: CANMSG1VAL
registers.title: CAN Message 1 Valid
notes: CANMSG1VAL holds the MSGVAL bits of message objects 1 to 16 and CANMSG2VAL those of objects 17 to 32. A MSGVAL bit is changed through CANIFnARB2.

fields.name: MSGVAL
fields.text: MSGVAL bit of each of the 16 message objects.

values.text: That message object is not set up and the message handler ignores it.
That message object is set up and the message handler takes it into account.

registers.name: CANMSG2VAL
registers.title: CAN Message 2 Valid
notes: CANMSG1VAL holds the MSGVAL bits of message objects 1 to 16 and CANMSG2VAL those of objects 17 to 32. A MSGVAL bit is changed through CANIFnARB2.

fields.name: MSGVAL
fields.text: MSGVAL bit of each of the 16 message objects.

values.text: That message object is not set up and the message handler ignores it.
That message object is set up and the message handler takes it into account.

fields.name: IN1
fields.text: Masked interrupt state of comparator 1; writing 1 clears it and ACRIS.IN1.

values.text: No interrupt, or the interrupt is masked.
IN1 is set in both ACRIS and ACINTEN, so the interrupt reaches the interrupt controller.

fields.name: IN0
fields.text: Masked interrupt state of comparator 0; writing 1 clears it and ACRIS.IN0.

values.text: No interrupt, or the interrupt is masked.
IN0 is set in both ACRIS and ACINTEN, so the interrupt reaches the interrupt controller.

registers.name: ACRIS
registers.title: Analog Comparator Raw Interrupt Status
notes: A bit here raises an interrupt only when enabled in ACINTEN.

fields.name: IN1
fields.text: Raw interrupt state of comparator 1; cleared by writing 1 to ACMIS.IN1.

values.text: Comparator 1 raised an interrupt for the event chosen by ACCTL1.ISEN.

fields.name: IN0
fields.text: Raw interrupt state of comparator 0; cleared by writing 1 to ACMIS.IN0.

values.text: Comparator 0 raised an interrupt for the event chosen by ACCTL0.ISEN.

fields.name: IN1
fields.text: Enables the comparator 1 interrupt.

values.text: A comparator 1 interrupt leaves the interrupt state unchanged.
The raw comparator 1 interrupt goes to the interrupt controller.

fields.name: IN0
fields.text: Enables the comparator 0 interrupt.

values.text: A comparator 0 interrupt leaves the interrupt state unchanged.
The raw comparator 0 interrupt goes to the interrupt controller.

fields.name: EN
fields.text: Powers the resistor ladder of the internal reference; 0 at reset, so an unused reference draws the least power.

fields.name: RNG
fields.text: Range of the resistor ladder.

values.text: Ideal step of the internal reference is VDDA / 29.4.
Ideal step of the internal reference is VDDA / 22.12.

fields.name: VREF
fields.text: Resistor ladder tap sent through an analog multiplexer; the tap voltage is the internal reference used for comparison.

fields.name: OVAL
fields.text: Present output of the comparator. VIN- is the Cn- pin; VIN+ is the Cn+ pin, the C0+ pin or the internal reference VIREF, as ACCTL.ASRCP selects.

fields.name: OVAL
fields.text: Present output of the comparator. VIN- is the Cn- pin; VIN+ is the Cn+ pin, the C0+ pin or the internal reference VIREF, as ACCTL.ASRCP selects.

fields.name: TOEN
fields.text: Lets comparator events reach the ADC.

values.text: ADC events go to the ADC.

fields.name: ASRCP
fields.text: Input for the comparator VIN+ terminal.

fields.name: TSLVAL
fields.text: Output level that raises an ADC event under level sense.

values.text: ADC event while the output is Low.
ADC event while the output is High.

fields.name: TSEN
fields.text: Which behaviour of the comparator output raises an ADC event.

fields.name: ISLVAL
fields.text: Output level that raises an interrupt under level sense.

values.text: Interrupt while the output is Low.
Interrupt while the output is High.
